ASUU backs Taraba varsity lecturers, demands strike resolutionBy
items.description: Femi Bolaji JALINGO – The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Yola Zone, has declared solidarity with lecturers of Taraba State University (TSU) over their ongoing strike, describing their grievances as legitimate and demanding immediate implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement. The union also urged the Taraba State Government to stop delaying the implementation of the agreed remuneration framework and settle outstanding arrears owed to the university’s academic staff. The Zonal Coordinator of ASUU, Comrade Dani Mamman, stated this while addressing journalists after an expanded congress meeting of the union in Jalingo. Mamman criticised the state government for what he described as unnecessary administrative delays, insisting that the grievances of the university’s lecturers deserved immediate attention. He said the zone’s support for ASUU-TSU was based on the principles of justice, equity, collective responsibility and the protection of the legitimate rights and entitlements of academic staff. The Yola Zone comprises seven public university branches across Adamawa, Borno, Taraba and Yobe states. They are Adamawa State University, Mubi; Federal University Gashua; Kashim Ibrahim University, Maiduguri; Modibbo Adama University, Yola; Taraba State University, Jalingo; University of Maiduguri; and Yobe State University, Damaturu. Mamman faulted the state government for placing Taraba State University lecturers in a different position from their counterparts in other universities in the region, urging it to end further delays. He said a report by the Taraba State Government’s fact-finding team, presented to ASUU on September 24, 2026, established that the universities covered by the exercise had fully implemented the 2025 FGN/ASUU agreement. According to him, the finding was particularly significant because other universities in the zone had adopted the payment tables provided under the agreement without undergoing similar fact-finding exercises. He said the state government had no justification for subjecting ASUU-TSU to further administrative processes after completing its verification exercise in August 2026. Mamman also expressed concern over what he described as endless computations by the government, particularly its consideration of alternative implementation levels of 95, 98 and 100 per cent after the verification exercise had been concluded. He maintained that consultations, negotiations and computations had been completed, leaving no reason for further delays. The zonal coordinator demanded the immediate and full implementation of the agreed remuneration framework without setting up additional committees or conducting further verification exercises. He also called for the settlement of all accumulated arrears based on the financial computations submitted by the tripartite committee. Other demands include strict adherence to the standard payment template stipulated in the 2025 agreement and immediate, meaningful engagement between the state government and ASUU-TSU in line with collective bargaining and mutual respect. The post ASUU backs Taraba varsity lecturers, demands strike resolutionBy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Japan: Raise Rights With Vietnam’s Leader
items.description: Click to expand Image Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (left) and Vietnamese President To Lam before a meeting in Hanoi, Vietnam, May 2, 2026. © 2026 Kyodo News via AP Photo (Tokyo) – Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi should urge Vietnamese President To Lam to make concrete progress on human rights during his official visit to Japan from November 8 to 11, 2026, Human Rights Watch said today. Human Rights Watch wrote to Prime Minister Takaichi expressing concerns about Vietnam’s intensifying crackdown on human rights. The repression violates obligations that Vietnam accepted under the 2018 Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, to which Vietnam and Japan are parties. “The Vietnamese government has broken its pledges for reform and continues to crack down on basic freedoms,” said Kanae Doi, Japan director at Human Rights Watch. “Prime Minister Takaichi should communicate clearly and publicly to President To Lam Japan’s serious concerns about human rights and labor rights violations.” The Vietnamese government has sharply intensified its repression of basic freedoms over the past decade, Human Rights Watch said. To Lam served as Vietnam’s minister of public security from 2016 to 2024, heading the country’s national police force. He is now both general secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam and president. Japan is among Vietnam’s top trade partners and one of the largest sources of foreign direct investment in the country. As Vietnam’s largest bilateral donor of development assistance for more than 20 years, and a major trade partner, Japan is in a very favorable position to persuade Vietnam to improve the country’s human rights. On To Lam’s watch, Vietnamese police initiated a far-reaching crackdown that decimated the country’s civil society, stepped up transnational repression, and expanded the scope and use of draconian laws that criminalize the exercise of freedom of expression, in contravention of international human rights law. Vietnam currently has more than 160 political prisoners, convicted under laws that violate their rights to free expression and peaceful activism for human rights and democracy. These include: Pham Doan Trang, a writer and human rights advocate; Can Thi Theu, a land rights activist; Pham Chi Dung and Nguyen Tuong Thuy, independent journalists; Hoang Duc Binh, a labor activist; and Le Dinh Luong, Nguyen Van Tuc, Tran Duc Thach, Tran Van Bang, and Nguyen Trung Ton, democracy campaigners. During the first nine months of 2026, Vietnamese courts convicted and sentenced at least 31 activists, including the prominent bloggers Hoang Thi Hong Thai and Huynh Ngoc Tuan, to long prison terms. Police arrested at least 46 other people for allegedly criticizing the government. The Vietnamese government has failed to put in place legal reforms it pledged to undertake, Human Rights Watch said. In article 19.3 of the Trans-Pacific Partnership, Vietnam committed to “adopt and maintain in its statutes and regulations, and practices thereunder,” the rights in the International Labour Organization (ILO) Declaration, including the “freedom of association and the effective recognition of the right to collective bargaining.” Vietnam also pledged to ratify ILO Convention No. 87 on Freedom of Association and Protection of the Right to Organise by January 2024 but has yet to do so and continues to thwart the establishment of independent trade unions. Japan’s own Diplomatic Bluebook 2026 states that the Trans-Pacific Partnership “has great strategic significance in that it will establish a free and fair economic order with countries sharing fundamental values and principles, including freedom, democracy, fundamental human rights and the rule of law,” values that the Vietnamese government has systematically disregarded. Japan has not meaningfully responded to Vietnam’s worsening human rights record. In November 2023, the two countries upgraded their relationship to the highest level, a “comprehensive strategic partnership for Peace and Prosperity in Asia and the World.” “Japan should stop giving Vietnam a free pass on repression,” Doi said. “As one of Vietnam’s most important partners, Japan should make clear to To Lam that respecting basic rights and its labor commitments are crucial for a strong and lasting partnership.”

items.title: Obi exhausted from campaign schedule, but in good health — NDC
items.description: The Deputy Spokesperson of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, Sam Omale, has said the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, is in good health, attributing concerns about his condition to exhaustion from a demanding campaign schedule. Omale said Obi had been advised to take some rest following hectic engagements involving frequent travels between cities and attendance at multiple political activities. He spoke on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Tuesday while responding to concerns about Obi’s health, particularly after his recent campaign rally in Enugu State, where he reportedly indicated plans to take a break. The campaign council’s deputy spokesperson described Obi as being in good health, insisting that the exhaustion would not affect his campaign activities. “If you know the person of Mr Peter Obi, he is so passionate for this country and he is pouring out his life. Sometimes, I wonder where he gets his energy from,” Omale said. “Today, he is in London this night; the following morning, he is in Enugu. The exhaustion comes in. A human being is a human being. “But he is in perfect health; nothing is wrong with him. It is just exhaustion, and we are trying to calm him down to take a sleep.” He said Obi often combined several activities at the same time, including attending engagements, answering questions and responding to emails. According to him, the former Anambra State governor would continue with town hall meetings before the commencement of the main campaign rallies. “So, it is pure exhaustion, which definitely has no impact on the campaign we are conducting. He is going to continue the town halls before the main rallies begin. He is fine,” Omale added. However, the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, said he was unaware that the party’s presidential candidate had experienced exhaustion arising from campaign activities. Director, who said he had spent time with Obi in Bayelsa State, maintained that he had no knowledge of any health-related incident involving the presidential candidate. “I knew nothing happened to Peter Obi. Honestly, I am not being sarcastic here. As far as I am concerned and as far as I know, Peter Obi is with his health,” he said. He added that he was with Obi in Bayelsa for a day and learnt that the presidential candidate had travelled abroad, noting that some people had accompanied him to the airport. “So, I don’t know where the story of exhaustion came from. So, Omale is in a better position to elucidate the point he has made,” he said. Director further said the national campaign council had not taken any steps to ask Obi to slow down his activities, adding that he was unaware of any development that would require such intervention. The post Obi exhausted from campaign schedule, but in good health — NDC appeared first on Vanguard News .

Alausa said he was familiar with the university, having lived in Chicago for almost 30 years, and had personally met several people who studied with Tinubu. He stated this during an interview on Channels Television on Tuesday while responding to questions about the President’s educational qualifications. “I’m telling you hardcore facts. I lived in Chicago for almost 30 years. I’ve been to that university so many times,” he said. Asked whether he had met Tinubu’s classmates, the minister replied, “Oh, many, many, many, in person. Many. So forget the nonsense of…” When asked whether the President graduated with a first-class degree from the institution, Alausa answered, “In accounting, of course.” He also described Tinubu as a genius, dismissing questions about the President’s intellectual capacity. “Oh, he’s a genius. Let’s not talk about the capability of this President. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is literally a genius,” he said. The minister further defended Tinubu’s performance in office, claiming that the President had transformed Nigeria from a moribund country into a growing economy. “Look at how he’s transformed a moribund country three years ago to a country that is growing,” Alausa said. However, when the interviewer challenged the description by pointing to the country’s out-of-school children and poverty levels, the minister insisted that the conversation should remain focused on the President’s achievements. “Let me focus on what you’re saying. I don’t want you to derail this conversation. But this President has delivered this for Nigeria,” he added. Tinubu’s academic qualifications have continued to attract public scrutiny, particularly following the controversy surrounding his Chicago State University records during the 2023 presidential election petition. The debate resurfaced in August 2026 after the Independent National Electoral Commission began displaying the personal particulars and academic credentials submitted by presidential candidates for the 2027 general elections. items.title: L’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods présente à Istanbul son initiative "Made for Palestine"
items.description: L’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods Acharif, bras exécutif du Comité Al-Qods, présidé par le Roi Mohammed VI, a présenté, mardi à Istanbul, son initiative “Made for Palestine”, en marge des travaux de la 42e session ministérielle du Comité permanent pour la coopération économique et commerciale (COMCEC) de l’Organisation de la coopération islamique (OCI). À cette occasion, le directeur chargé de la gestion de l’Agence, Mohamed Salem Cherkaoui, qui a rencontré les chefs de plusieurs délégations participant à cette session, a indiqué que l’Agence a placé son plan d’action à Al-Qods pour l’année en cours sous le thème “La dynamisation de l’économie palestinienne à Al-Qods, levier de développement et de stabilité sociale”. Cherkaoui a présenté aux chefs de délégation l’initiative “Made for Palestine”, que l’Agence prévoit de lancer après l’adoption de sa Vision 2030 et de son programme d’action 2027-2030. Cette initiative, a-t-il expliqué, permettra aux entreprises, aux marques commerciales, aux coopératives et aux artisans, dans le monde islamique et au-delà, de soutenir l’économie d’Al-Qods en consacrant une partie du produit de leurs ventes au financement des programmes de l’Agence dans la Ville sainte. S’inscrivant dans la Vision 2030 de l’Agence, cette initiative vise à mobiliser durablement le secteur privé en faveur de l’économie maqdessie, en offrant aux entreprises et aux consommateurs un mécanisme fiable et transparent pour soutenir la Ville sainte à travers leurs activités commerciales et leurs achats, a-t-il ajouté. Il a également précisé que l’initiative repose sur deux volets. Le premier concerne des produits arborant des motifs et des symboles inspirés de la Palestine, soumis à une homologation spécifique avant leur commercialisation, tandis que le second permet aux marques commerciales de consacrer une part convenue du produit de leurs ventes au soutien des programmes de l’Agence. Cherkaoui a, en outre, expliqué que l’initiative “Made for Palestine” reposera sur une plateforme numérique permettant aux entreprises de soumettre leurs demandes de participation, de présenter les marques et les produits labellisés et de vérifier l’authenticité du label grâce à un numéro de licence et un code QR. Elle permettra également de suivre les déclarations de ventes et les transferts financiers afin de garantir la transparence et la traçabilité des contributions. Par ailleurs, Mohamed Salem Cherkaoui a présenté les actions menées par l’Agence en faveur de l’économie et du commerce, en partenariat avec la Chambre de commerce et d’industrie arabe d’Al-Qods, notamment pour accompagner les commerçants locaux, soutenir les start-up palestiniennes, développer les compétences professionnelles et artisanales et aider les jeunes à créer et à développer leurs projets. À cet égard, il a indiqué que le programme “Incubateur de start-up” a soutenu, en 2025 et 2026, un total de 34 start-up réparties en six groupes, dont huit ont bénéficié de programmes d’accélération, tandis que trois autres ont développé leurs activités commerciales en Italie et aux Émirats arabes unis. Il a également rappelé que l’Agence a soutenu, en avril dernier, la participation de six start-up palestiniennes au salon “GITEX Africa”, organisé à Marrakech, leur permettant de présenter leurs produits et services, d’établir des contacts avec des investisseurs et des partenaires, ainsi que d’explorer les possibilités de coopération et d’accès aux marchés régionaux et internationaux. En juillet dernier, l’Agence a également organisé quatre sessions de formation à l’importation et à l’exportation au profit d’une centaine de commerçants maqdessis, afin de renforcer leurs compétences commerciales et de les aider à mieux gérer leurs activités et leurs relations avec les marchés, a-t-il ajouté. Cherkaoui a également évoqué un programme de formation à l’artisanat marocain, organisé par l’Agence au profit de 38 stagiaires, sous l’encadrement de trois artisans marocains. Consacré au tissage, à la sculpture sur bois et au travail du cuivre et de l’argent, ce programme vise à transmettre les savoir-faire artisanaux, à préserver le patrimoine artisanal et à renforcer les compétences professionnelles des participants. Le 42è session du COMCEC, qui se déroule sur deux jours, examine les évolutions économiques mondiales et la situation des pays membres de l’Organisation, ainsi que le développement d’un secteur touristique durable et compétitif. Les participants débattent également des moyens d’accroître la productivité du secteur agricole, de garantir la sécurité alimentaire et de réduire la pauvreté, outre le renforcement de la coopération dans le domaine de la transformation numérique. The post L’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods présente à Istanbul son initiative "Made for Palestine" appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Cnot | Perspectives de coopération prometteuses pour le volleyball tunisien
items.description: En marge des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse Dakar2026, M. Mehrez Boussayene, membre du Comité International Olympique (CIO) et président du Comité National Olympique Tunisien (Cnot),a rencontré, hier novembre à Dakar, M. Fabio Azevedo, président de la Fédération Internationale de Volleyball (FIVB). Cette rencontre a eu lieu en présence de Mme Bouchra Hajij, présidente de la Confédération Africaine de Volleyball (CAVB), M. Hitesh Malhotra, responsable du programme Volleyball Empowerment et des relations avec les fédérations nationales, et Anna Manuelian, responsable des affaires internationales et de la communication à la FIVB. Placée sous le signe de la coopération et de la solidarité sportives, la rencontre a porté sur les perspectives de renforcement du partenariat entre la FIVB et la Fédération Tunisienne de Volleyball, à la suite de la brillante qualification de l’équipe nationale masculine aux Jeux Olympiques de Los Angeles 2028, grâce à son récent titre de championne d’Afrique. À cette occasion, le président de la FIVB a renouvelé ses chaleureuses félicitations à la Tunisie pour cette performance et exprimé la pleine disposition de la Fédération Internationale à accompagner le développement du volleyball tunisien. Les échanges ont permis d’identifier les opportunités de coopération et de soutien, portant sur les équipements, la préparation des équipes nationales, l’encadrement technique et le développement du beach-volley. M. Mehrez Boussayene a exprimé ses vifs remerciements et sa profonde reconnaissance à M. Fabio Azevedo ainsi qu’à Mme Bouchra Hajij pour leur disponibilité, leur engagement et leur précieux soutien au volleyball tunisien. Cette rencontre illustre toute la portée de la coopération internationale et de la diplomatie sportive, lorsqu’elles se traduisent par des initiatives au bénéfice des fédérations nationales, des athlètes et du développement du sport. Un amigo le hablaba de un viaje de estudiantes a la isla canaria, previsto para ese verano, y él contestaba entre bromas: “Si me chivas y apruebo todas me voy a Tenerife”. Trece años después, Tenerife era su casa y el Heliodoro Rodríguez López, su estadio. items.title: SIAO 2026 : Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo encourage les artisans à repousser les limites de la créativité
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, accompagné d'une délégation gouvernementale et de la ministre de l'Artisanat du Congo, a effectué une visite au Salon international de l'artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO). Elle a eu lieu ce mardi 3 novembre 2026. Cette visite a été l'occasion pour le chef du gouvernement de découvrir les œuvres exposées, d'apprécier le savoir-faire des artisans africains et de les encourager à poursuivre leurs efforts de créativité et d'innovation. Au fil des stands, la délégation a pu apprécier la diversité des objets présentés, mais également le travail de finition et le raffinement des productions artisanales. Des créations qui témoignent, selon le Premier ministre, de la capacité des artisans africains à valoriser leur patrimoine tout en s'adaptant aux exigences de leur époque. « Nous avons été témoins de la créativité et du raffinement des objets », a-t-il souligné à l'issue de la visite. Pour Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, l'artisanat africain se distingue notamment par sa capacité à conjuguer authenticité culturelle et modernité. Il estime que les artisans parviennent à puiser dans les traditions, les valeurs et le patrimoine africains tout en proposant des créations adaptées aux tendances contemporaines. « L'artisanat s'inspire de nos traditions, de nos valeurs et de notre patrimoine, mais l'artisanat doit être de son temps. C'est une équation que les artisans arrivent à résoudre », a-t-il souligné. Le chef du gouvernement a également salué la qualité des finitions observées sur les différentes productions. Une évolution qui, à ses yeux, témoigne du potentiel et du génie créateur des artisans du continent. « De plus en plus, les artisans africains n'ont rien à envier à qui que ce soit », a-t-il dit. Le premier ministre Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo Au-delà de la découverte des œuvres, cette visite se voulait aussi un message d'encouragement à l'endroit des exposants. Le Premier ministre les a invités à maintenir cette dynamique de créativité et à poursuivre la recherche de la qualité dans leurs productions. Convaincu des perspectives qu'offre ce secteur, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo a rappelé que l'artisanat constitue un domaine porteur d'avenir. Il a, par ailleurs, invité les amoureux des belles créations à faire le déplacement au SIAO afin de découvrir la richesse du savoir-faire africain. À travers cette visite, le chef du gouvernement a ainsi mis en avant la nécessité de préserver l'authenticité des productions artisanales africaines, tout en encourageant leur adaptation aux évolutions contemporaines. Rama Diallo Lefaso.net

items.title: 2027: Opposition criticism won’t weaken Tinubu’s Northern support — Illiyasu Kwankwaso
items.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse An influential member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Musa Illiyasu Kwankwaso, has dismissed opposition criticism of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, insisting that it would not weaken the President’s support base in northern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kwankwaso said supporters of Tinubu in the North remained committed to his re-election bid despite sustained criticism from opposition politicians. He stated this on Tuesday while hosting journalists in Dutse, the Jigawa State capital, where he described Tinubu as the right candidate for the 2027 presidential election. “There is no panic and no going back in our support for Tinubu. The criticisms coming from the opposition will not stop us from voting for him in the North,” he said. The APC chieftain described the opposition’s criticism as part of political manoeuvring ahead of the 2027 elections, arguing that political rhetoric alone would not diminish what he characterised as the President’s growing support across the region. According to him, northern voters are increasingly concerned about issues directly affecting their lives, including economic recovery, security, infrastructure development, employment and national stability. He maintained that the administration’s policies, programmes and achievements since assuming office had strengthened confidence among its supporters, although he did not provide specific indicators to substantiate the claim. Kwankwaso said supporters of the President would intensify grassroots mobilisation across northern communities to communicate the administration’s policies and highlight what they consider its achievements. He urged APC members not to be distracted by opposition narratives but to concentrate on strengthening party structures and maintaining regular engagement with voters ahead of the elections. The APC stalwart expressed confidence that the political coalition backing Tinubu would remain united and focused, adding that supporters were prepared to defend the administration’s record and seek a fresh mandate based on its performance. He called on Tinubu’s supporters across northern Nigeria to remain committed, describing the 2027 elections as an opportunity to sustain ongoing government policies and programmes and give the President more time to consolidate his administration’s development agenda. items.title: 2027: Akume’s allies disown Alia’s campaign council as Benue APC supremacy war deepens
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A fresh supremacy battle has erupted in the Benue State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, following the rejection of about 500-man campaign council for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Hyacinth Alia by the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, a political mobilisation platform associated with the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume. The disagreement followed Monday’s announcement by the APC State Organising Secretary, James Ornguga, of a joint campaign council for Tinubu and Alia ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also fixed Thursday, November 5, for the inauguration of the council in Makurdi, with a supplementary list expected to be released later. However, the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, in a disclaimer issued Tuesday and signed by its Director-General, Chief Akange Audu, disowned the purported campaign structure, alleging that the names of its conveners, members and political candidates had been included without their authorisation. The Alliance specifically faulted the inclusion of its conveners, Senator Jack Tilley-Gyado, and Elder Simon Shango, as well as its candidates for the National Assembly and Benue State House of Assembly, in the list of the purported Alia campaign council. It stated, “for the avoidance of doubt, the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027 categorically dissociates itself from the said publication and disowns any claim or suggestion that the individuals mentioned therein are associated with, or constitute members of, the purported Alia Campaign structure.” The group further questioned the political arrangement that reportedly placed Governor Alia as chairman of the campaign council while listing Akume, whom it described as the founder and foremost political leader of the APC in Benue State, as merely a member. According to the Alliance, “We find it particularly contentious that a purported Alia Campaign structure would designate Governor Hyacinth Alia as its Chairman while listing the Founder and foremost political leader of the APC in Benue State, Sen. George Akume, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, merely as a member.” The Akume-aligned group alleged that “since the APC secured victory in the 2023 general elections, the party’s established leadership and structures have, in practical terms, been sidelined by the Alia administration. This has contributed to the divisions and disagreements currently affecting the party in the state.” Despite rejecting the campaign council, the group insisted that “the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027 remains committed to its stated mandate of mobilising support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. “Our political engagement also extends to supporting APC candidates for the National Assembly and the Benue State House of Assembly who emerge from the list and leadership direction recognised by our leader, Sen. George Akume.” The Alliance also took a swipe at the Alia-led administration, saying “we remain concerned about the hardship experienced by the people of Benue State under the present administration of Governor Hyacinth Alia. We believe that the 2027 political process should provide an opportunity for constructive engagement on governance, accountability, party unity and the welfare of our people. “The Alliance is an independent and clearly structured political mobilisation platform. Its identity, leadership and membership cannot be appropriated, manipulated or misrepresented through unauthorised publications. “We therefore urge APC State, Local Government, Ward Executives, stakeholders, members and the general public to disregard the purported publication.” The post 2027: Akume’s allies disown Alia’s campaign council as Benue APC supremacy war deepens appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lebanon cocaine bust: Three foreign nationals arrested in Ghana
items.description: Three foreign nationals — a Syrian, a Tunisian and a Lebanese — have been arrested in Ghana in connection with the seizure of 46.7 kilogrammes of cocaine at the Rafic Hariri International Airport in Beirut, Lebanon. The arrests form part of investigations into the movement of the consignment from Accra to Beirut and efforts to identify others suspected of involvement in the international drug trafficking network. JoyNews sources said the suspects, comprising two men and a woman, were picked up in separate operations on Tuesday, November 3. Two were arrested earlier in the day in Accra, while the third was apprehended at about 5 p.m. They were arrested by the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) following intelligence shared by Lebanese law enforcement authorities. The suspects are being investigated to establish the extent of their alleged involvement in the shipment and the wider trafficking network. Cocaine concealed in luggage The investigation follows the arrest of a Syrian national at Beirut’s Rafic Hariri International Airport on Saturday, October 31, after he arrived from Accra with cocaine concealed in two pieces of luggage. Lebanese Customs authorities said officers discovered 40 packages containing a total of 46.7 kilogrammes of cocaine during a search of the passenger’s luggage. The drugs were reportedly concealed using sophisticated packaging and insulation materials intended to evade detection by scanning equipment. Electronic tracking devices were also found among the packages. Lebanese authorities described the seizure as the largest drug bust in the history of the airport. Preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect had entered Lebanon through the Masnaa border crossing from Syria several weeks earlier before travelling to Accra and returning with the consignment. The authorities said investigations were continuing to identify the intended recipient of the drugs and to trace those who had organised and facilitated the shipment. NACOC has maintained that the arrest in Lebanon resulted from a coordinated controlled-delivery operation involving Ghanaian and Lebanese drug law enforcement agencies. In a statement issued on November 1, the commission said the operation was intended to identify and apprehend individuals at both ends of the supply chain while gathering intelligence to dismantle the wider transnational criminal network. It also said it was pursuing suspected accomplices in Ghana.

items.title: Youth Forum backs Audi, warns against removal campaign
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Patriotic Nigeria Youth Forum (PNYF) has passed a vote of confidence on the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Prof. Ahmed Abubakar Audi, warning that campaigns for his removal could undermine ongoing reforms and efforts to protect the nation’s critical infrastructure. The forum said leadership continuity was important to consolidating the gains recorded by the Corps in professionalism, operational capacity and institutional development. National Coordinator of PNYF, Comrade Olamide Odumosu, stated the position during the forum’s 2026 National Youth Day celebration, held under the theme, “Reimagining the Nigerian Youth: Leadership, Innovation and a Greater Nation.” Odumosu specifically cautioned individuals and groups, including Mr Deji Adeyanju, reportedly campaigning for Audi’s removal, urging them to support their concerns with verifiable evidence rather than engage in activities capable of distracting the security agency from its statutory responsibilities. He said decisions concerning the leadership of a strategic security institution should be guided by measurable performance, facts and the national interest. According to him, the NSCDC has recorded improvements under Audi, particularly in protecting critical national assets, including oil and gas facilities, electricity installations, telecommunications infrastructure and other strategic public facilities. “Before our eyes, the NSCDC under Prof. Ahmed Abubakar Audi has undergone remarkable transformation. The Corps has moved beyond its previous limitations and is increasingly demonstrating the professionalism, discipline and operational capacity expected of a modern security institution,” he said. Odumosu added that Audi had demonstrated an understanding of institutional development and the strategic importance of protecting infrastructure vital to Nigeria’s economic stability and national security. “These achievements deserve recognition and encouragement,” he said. The forum maintained that sustained leadership could help consolidate ongoing reforms, particularly as the protection of critical infrastructure remained central to the country’s security and economic development. It urged those dissatisfied with the Commandant-General’s leadership to channel their grievances through constructive engagement and evidence-based criticism rather than campaigns it said could generate unnecessary distractions. Odumosu also expressed support for President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, describing the protection of critical national assets as an important component of efforts to strengthen national security and stimulate economic growth. He called on Nigerians, particularly young people, to support security agencies and recognise the contributions of personnel working to protect lives, property and essential infrastructure. Forum seeks greater investment in youths Beyond the debate over the NSCDC leadership, the forum called on the Federal Government and private sector to increase investment in skills development, entrepreneurship and employment opportunities for young Nigerians. Odumosu identified unemployment, poverty, inadequate access to quality education, insecurity and limited economic opportunities as major challenges confronting the country’s youth. He urged the government to prioritise digital skills, artificial intelligence, vocational education, research, entrepreneurship and greater youth participation in governance. The PNYF coordinator also challenged private companies to expand opportunities for young people through employment, internships, mentorship schemes, innovation grants and enterprise development programmes. “Investing in young people is not charity; it is an investment in Nigeria’s economic growth, stability and prosperity,” he said. He stressed that addressing the challenges facing young Nigerians required sustained collaboration among government institutions, businesses and civil society organisations. Odumosu reaffirmed the forum’s commitment to promoting responsible citizenship, leadership development, patriotism, innovation and national unity. He also urged young Nigerians to embrace peaceful democratic participation, respect for the rule of law and active involvement in national development, saying the country’s future depended significantly on their contributions towards building a secure and prosperous nation. items.title: Kankan : 60 cartons de produits de chicha saisis par la police, les propriétaires recherchés
items.description: La police de Kankan a saisi 60 cartons de produits liés à la chicha, dissimulés dans 15 sacs abandonnés près de la gare routière de Farako 2. Les marchandises ont été présentées à la presse ce mardi 3 novembre 2026 au commissariat central. C’est une patrouille de routine qui a permis de mettre la main sur une importante cargaison. Quinze sacs de 150 kg, déposés sans surveillance au bord de la route, contenaient au total 50 cartons de charbon de chicha de marque Black Tiger et 10 cartons d’arômes de marque JBR. L’opération a été menée par la Brigade spéciale d’intervention de la police (BSIP) dans le quartier Farako 2. La découverte a eu lieu non loin de la gare routière, dans des circonstances encore floues, les propriétaires des colis restant introuvables. Cette saisie s’inscrit dans le cadre de la lutte contre l’importation, la distribution et la commercialisation de la chicha en Guinée, conformément à l’arrêté conjoint du 5 janvier 2021 portant interdiction de ces activités sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Selon le commissaire central de police de Kankan, Nanamoudou Magassouba, l’intervention fait suite à une réquisition du procureur de la République près le Tribunal de première instance de Kankan. « Notre service a été requis par monsieur le procureur de la République près le tribunal de première instance de Kankan, suivant la réquisition numéro 440/Parquet/2026, en date du 13 octobre 2026, pour rechercher, constater, saisir et inventorier les produits, appareils et accessoires liés à la chicha », a-t-il expliqué lors de la présentation à la presse. Revenant sur les circonstances de la découverte, le commissaire central a précisé : « Au cours de notre patrouille, la Brigade spéciale d’intervention de la police a constaté la présence de 15 sacs de 150 kg déposés au bord de la route, non loin de la gare routière du quartier Farako 2. Nos investigations n’ont permis d’obtenir aucune information sur les propriétaires de ces colis, encore moins sur leur provenance ou leur destination. » Après inventaire, les services de police ont dénombré 50 cartons de charbon de chicha de marque Black Tiger et 10 cartons d’arômes de marque JBR, emballés dans les 15 sacs retrouvés sur les lieux. Le parquet a été immédiatement informé de la saisie et a autorisé l’ouverture d’une enquête. « Nous avons saisi les colis comprenant 50 cartons de charbon de chicha de marque Black Tiger et 10 cartons d’arômes de marque JBR, emballés dans les 15 sacs. Sans désemparer, nous avons informé monsieur le procureur de la République près le tribunal de première instance de Kankan, qui nous a autorisés à ouvrir une enquête afin d’interpeller les suspects et leurs éventuels complices », a déclaré le commissaire Magassouba. La procédure va se poursuivre devant les juridictions compétentes. « Après cette saisie, nous allons établir un rapport de synthèse et le déposer au greffe du tribunal de première instance de Kankan », a-t-il annoncé. Cette nouvelle opération témoigne de l’intensification des actions engagées par les services de sécurité contre la circulation des produits liés à la chicha dans la région de Kankan. Les investigations se poursuivent afin d’identifier les propriétaires des marchandises et de faire toute la lumière sur cette affaire. Karifa Kansan Doumbouya correspondant à Kankan L’article Kankan : 60 cartons de produits de chicha saisis par la police, les propriétaires recherchés est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Rising feed costs threaten poultry, livestock farming in 3 states
items.description: Farmers in Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states have warned that rising feed costs, expensive day-old chicks and poor market prices threaten livestock production and livelihoods. They said the situation had forced some operators to reduce production, sell their animals at losses or abandon farming altogether. The farmers spoke in separate interviews with the News Agency of Nigeria on Tuesday during a nationwide survey in Minna. They identified high feed costs, which account for 70 to 80 per cent of poultry production expenses, as their biggest challenge. They called for subsidised feed ingredients, affordable financing, improved access to essential inputs and local feed mills to reduce production costs. In Kogi, a poultry farmer and retired Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security director, Mr Dare Olukaiyeja, said feeding accounted for 80 per cent of his production costs. Olukaiyeja, who keeps 250 birds, said a crate of eggs currently sold for about N6,200 amid declining consumer purchasing power. Similarly, Mr Shola Adeyi, a Lokoja-based farmer with a 1,000-bird capacity, said feed prices had increased by N2,000 to N3,000 per bag almost monthly since January. He said starter, finisher and layer feeds sold for N22,500, N22,000 and N16,000 respectively, while day-old chicks cost about N2,200 each. Adeyi identified unreliable electricity, extreme heat and high bird mortality as additional challenges confronting poultry farmers. He said some operators had abandoned the business because they could not afford alternative power sources. He said eggs sold for between N6,000 and N6,500 per crate, while broilers fetched N4,500 to N5,000 per kilogramme. According to him, the prices barely covered production costs, necessitating long-term subsidised or interest-free loans and effective market regulation. Another farmer, Mr Malik Ajayi, said day-old chick and feed prices usually increased during Sallah, Easter and Christmas. Ajayi, who rears broilers, cockerels and foreign turkeys, said he recently bought three cartons of day-old chicks for N352,500. He attributed some price fluctuations to possible exploitation by large-scale producers and urged the government to introduce effective price regulation. Ajayi, who keeps 150 broilers, 50 cockerels and 15 foreign turkeys, said some farmers sold their birds cheaply to avoid prolonged feeding costs. He added that frozen poultry dealers also faced high electricity and preservation expenses. Mrs Oluwaseyi Fadaka, another Lokoja-based farmer, said a bag of feed now cost about N22,000, with her 40 Noiler birds consuming one regularly. She said rising feeding costs were eroding profits, forcing farmers to sell at losses or abandon the business. Fadaka said some smallholders were exploring organic feeding alternatives but needed government support through subsidised feed and affordable, quality inputs. Responding, the Kogi Government said it was implementing interventions through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES). The State Project Coordinator, Mr Abdulkabir Otaru, said the World Bank-supported project targeted productivity, commercialisation and resilience across livestock value chains. He said the project recently supported 500 women and youths across the state’s 21 local government areas with poultry inputs and equipment. Beneficiaries also received day-old chicks, feed, drugs, vaccines and N100,000 each for logistics support. The Commissioner for Livestock Development, Dr Olufemi Bolarin, said the ministry was collaborating with L-PRES and stakeholders on sustainable solutions. He said improved poultry breeds, including resilient, dual-purpose SASSO chickens, were being introduced to strengthen food security and farmers’ incomes. Stakeholders called for subsidised maize and soya beans, local feed ingredient production and solar power support to reduce bird mortality. In Niger, poultry farmers and feed dealers said rising feed, chick and transportation costs were threatening the sustainability of poultry businesses. A NAN survey at Firduas Agrovet, a poultry feed and day-old chick dealership in Minna, revealed significant increases in poultry input prices. The dealers attributed the increases largely to rising transportation costs, saying some feed prices had risen by about 40 per cent over the previous year. They said a bag of layer feed, previously sold for N7,500 to N8,000, now cost about N15,000. Broiler feed, formerly sold for approximately N18,000, had increased to N24,000, they added. A day-old broiler chick sold for N2,200, while a layer chick cost about N3,500, with festive demand influencing prices. The dealers said N500,000, which previously could sustain about 500 birds, could now cater for only approximately 100. A poultry farmer, Mr Bala Ibrahim, said rising production costs and unstable market prices were making it difficult to sustain businesses. He said feed constituted a significant proportion of production expenses, while fluctuating chick prices complicated financial planning. Ibrahim said some operators had reduced their flock sizes, while others struggled to remain in business. He said poultry sales frequently failed to cover feeding, medication, labour, transportation and other production expenses. He urged the Niger government to reduce production costs and improve farmers’ access to affordable feed and essential inputs. Responding, the Permanent Secretary, Niger Ministry for Livestock, Mr Jonathan Wasa, said the government planned to revive and upgrade the Tagwai feed mill. He said the initiative was intended to improve local feed availability and reduce the financial pressure on livestock farmers. Wasa said the ministry was collaborating with Niger Foods to facilitate the supply of raw materials for feed production. He explained that feed transported from Kaduna and Ilorin was expensive because of additional transportation and distribution costs. Establishing local feed production, he said, would reduce dependence on external supplies and improve accessibility. Wasa said Niger had abundant raw materials for feed production, adding that the government was working to harness the resources. He expressed optimism that upgrading the Tagwai facility would improve feed availability and reduce production costs when operations began. He said the intervention would strengthen the livestock value chain and create opportunities for farmers and agricultural input suppliers. In Nasarawa, livestock farmers also blamed rising feed costs and poor market prices for declining profitability and farm closures. The farmers spoke to NAN in Lafia, citing rising maize and soya bean prices without corresponding increases in poultry product prices. A poultry farmer, Mr Musa Ibrahim, said feed accounted for about 70 per cent of production expenses. “The cost of feed constitutes about 70 per cent of production. We are buying feed at exorbitant prices but selling at a loss because consumers cannot afford high prices. “Many of our members have closed their farms. If nothing is done urgently, poultry and livestock farming will collapse in the state,” he said. Mrs Sarah Audu, a livestock farmer from Akwanga, said high feed costs had forced her to reduce her flock from 2,000 birds to 500. She urged the state and federal governments to provide subsidised feed ingredients and establish feed mills. Similarly, Alhaji Suleiman Danlami, a cattle fattener in Keffi, decried poor animal prices in spite of rising production costs. “During festive periods we expect to make profit, but now even at Sallah and Christmas, prices are poor. Transportation cost is high, feed is high, but market price is low,” he said. The farmers warned that without urgent interventions to reduce production costs and improve market conditions, more smallholder operators could abandon livestock farming. They urged governments to strengthen local feed ingredient production, establish feed mills and provide affordable financing to sustain production and improve food security. items.title: JP Morgan’s Nigeria expansion to boost foreign investment — IMPI
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Independent Media and Policy Initiative (IMPI) has said the planned expansion of global financial giant JP Morgan Chase into Nigeria’s merchant banking sector could attract fresh foreign investments, improve corporate financing and strengthen the country’s access to international capital markets. The policy think tank said the American financial institution’s application for a national merchant banking licence was a significant endorsement of Nigeria’s investment prospects and could encourage more multinational corporations to commit long-term capital to the country. In a policy statement signed by its Chairman, Dr Omoniyi Akinsiju, IMPI said the proposed expansion could reshape Nigeria’s corporate finance landscape by making it easier for businesses to access funding, structure large-scale projects and manage risks associated with cross-border investments. According to the group, JP Morgan’s transition from a representative office to a fully licensed merchant bank would enable it to deepen its involvement in trade finance, corporate lending, cross-border underwriting and other sophisticated financial transactions. It said the development could be particularly beneficial to capital-intensive sectors such as energy, telecommunications and manufacturing, where high borrowing costs and complex financing arrangements had continued to constrain investments. “JP Morgan Chase’s move to secure a national merchant banking licence in Nigeria marks a significant shift in West Africa’s corporate finance landscape,” IMPI said. The group added that the proposed operations could help multinational companies structure investments more efficiently through direct access to cross-border trade facilities, commodity hedging instruments and syndicated financing involving domestic and international markets. It said the availability of such services could reduce delays and additional costs businesses often encounter when relying on multiple financial intermediaries to execute major projects. IMPI also argued that Nigeria’s sovereign and corporate borrowers could benefit from stronger links to international capital markets, while the presence of a major global financial institution could reinforce confidence among foreign pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and private equity investors. However, the think tank cautioned that JP Morgan’s proposed entry would not automatically translate into increased foreign direct investment, stressing that the broader benefits would depend on prevailing investment conditions and the consistency of economic policies. Tinubu’s reforms and investor confidence The policy group attributed renewed international interest in Nigeria to the economic policy direction of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, particularly the foreign exchange market reforms and removal of petrol subsidy introduced in 2023. It acknowledged that the reforms initially triggered inflationary pressures and currency depreciation but argued that they had helped reshape the country’s external financial position and renew international investor interest. “Our analysis found that the near four years of the federal administration mark a record of consistent current account surpluses, underpinned by an aggressive strategy to not only drive FDI but also link it to domestic macroeconomic stability with a medium- to long-term microeconomic impact,” the statement said. IMPI maintained that the reforms represented a structural shift from policies that previously distorted market signals towards a system intended to improve price discovery, strengthen external balances and attract sustainable investments. It said the emerging challenge was to convert renewed international interest and short-term capital inflows into investments that would expand productive capacity, create jobs and strengthen the real economy. From portfolio inflows to long-term investments The think tank also identified a potential shift in Nigeria’s foreign investment profile, arguing that the country could gradually move away from excessive dependence on foreign portfolio investments towards more sustainable foreign direct investments. It explained that portfolio investors had been attracted by high yields on government securities and other short-term financial instruments, while the Central Bank of Nigeria’s monetary and foreign exchange policies sought to address currency pressures and rebuild investor confidence. It noted that the surge in portfolio inflows had helped boost Nigeria’s foreign reserves to more than $55 billion, although the high interest rates associated with the strategy had also increased borrowing costs for domestic businesses. “For nearly two years, foreign capital prioritised government debt and Treasury bills (FPI) over physical infrastructure (FDI) because short-term paper yielded safely above 25 per cent,” IMPI said. The group argued that as inflation moderates and yields on fixed-income securities decline, investors could become more interested in longer-term opportunities, including infrastructure concessions, industrial projects and direct equity investments. It added that the declining attractiveness of short-term financial instruments could encourage institutional investors and cross-border private equity firms to redirect some of their funds towards productive assets. “For our standpoint, as inflation begins to moderate, the focus is shifting towards converting these temporary portfolio flows into permanent, factory-to-market FDI,” the statement added. IMPI said JP Morgan’s proposed merchant banking operations could facilitate this transition by providing the financing structures and risk-management instruments required to execute large-scale investments. It argued that international investors required more than favourable policy announcements before committing capital to physical projects, noting that predictable financing arrangements, credible risk-sharing mechanisms and access to institutions capable of handling complex transactions were equally important. The group said the presence of a globally influential financial institution could help bridge that gap by connecting Nigerian businesses and projects with international capital providers. It added that improved access to corporate finance could support investments in energy infrastructure, telecommunications and industrial production, while making it easier for Nigerian companies to participate in international trade. However, IMPI said the broader impact would depend on the consistency of economic reforms, the evolution of borrowing costs and the ability of businesses to translate improved financing opportunities into viable projects. It maintained that JP Morgan’s proposed expansion should be viewed not merely as the arrival of another financial institution, but as an opportunity to deepen Nigeria’s integration into global investment networks. The group said the ultimate test would be whether renewed investor attention translated into factories, infrastructure, expanded production and jobs rather than remaining concentrated in short-term financial instruments. For Nigeria, it added, the opportunity lay in converting improving investor sentiment into sustained capital formation capable of supporting long-term economic growth. The post JP Morgan’s Nigeria expansion to boost foreign investment — IMPI appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘My expectations are much higher’ – Fifi Kwetey gives government 7/10
items.description: NDC General Secretary Fifi Fiavi Kwetey has rated his party’s performance in government 7/10, saying he expects more despite giving it a passing score. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, he said the government should aim higher. “Maybe because my expectations are much higher, for now I will give it seven.” He described the score as “more than a pass” but made clear that it was no reason to settle, saying, “I expect us to push for more.” When asked for his ideal mark, Mr Kwetey replied, “10 out of 10.” He acknowledged that a perfect score would be difficult. Still, he wanted performance to improve towards the eight-out-of-10 range. His assessment came alongside questions about accountability. The interviewer cited allegations involving World Cup visas and the National Sports Authority head being asked to step aside. Mr Kwetey said he had never expected the government to complete its term without problems. He argued the real test was how leaders responded. “There’s no government on the planet that could go four years without having a difficulty.” “But the difference is what leadership does when things of that nature emerge.” He said party membership offered no guarantee that an official would uphold the values they professed. “As I told you, the party is not made up of angels. It’s humans.” Mr Kwetey insisted that protecting the party should not mean shielding individuals accused of wrongdoing. He said the leadership must be prepared to act against officials, regardless of their position. “You take a tough decision. You deal with them, no matter who they are, whether they are ministers or they are CEOs.” Drawing a distinction between the NDC and the NPP, he accused the previous administration of defending wrongdoing. He maintained that the current leadership would respond differently. “Under us, if it happens, we will deal with you.”

items.title: Champions League: Man United rise from the dust to shock Roma 3-2
items.description: Manchester United roared back from 2-0 down to give beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a lifeline with a memorable 3-2 win over Roma at Old Trafford. The unrest among the home fans bordered on mutiny after Roma surged into a 2-0 lead inside 20 minutes through Matias Soule and Donyell Malen. But Matheus Cunha’s struck twice after a twice-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty had given United hope to end a nine-game winless run in all competitions. The decision to hand Carrick a stay of execution looked to have backfired in a lifeless first half United performance. Roma, though, failed to slay their ghosts of previous trips to Old Trafford in another spectacular Champions League collapse. Gian Piero Gasperini’s lost 4-3 to Real Madrid last month after leading 3-1 with just eight minutes remaining. The Italians have now lost on all five visits to the Theatre of Dreams, most notably when Carrick scored twice in a 7-1 thrashing in the Champions League quarter-finals 19 years ago. Carrick reacted to Lisandro Martinez’s foolish red card in a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday by dropping the Argentine international. It made little difference as his disorganised defence was torn apart inside the opening 20 minutes. Soule was afforded acres of space to control Rodrigo Mora’s pass and slot past Senne Lammens on 11 minutes. Moments later United were left completely exposed again down their left and Soule’s shot hit the outstretched hand of Ayden Heaven. Malen converted the resulting penalty for his 12th goal of the season. The game was temporarily stopped midway through the first half by supporters throwing tennis balls onto the field, accompanied by chants calling for with United’s unpopular owners, the American-based Glazer family, to sell the club. United were dealt a further blow inside two minutes of the second half when £70 million ($94 million) signing Carlos Baleba pulled up with a suspected severe hamstring injury after bursting into the Roma box. Yet, Carrick’s luck turned just before the hour mark when Cunha won a generous penalty award for minimal contact by Gianluca Mancini. Fernandes’s first spot-kick was saved by Roma’s third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez, but was given a reprieve by encroaching by the visitors. The United captain smashed home at the second attempt to kickstart the comeback. Seconds later Bryan Mbeumo hit the inside of both posts and Roma captain Bryan Cristante had to hack clear off the line as the visitors rode their luck. However, Leonardo Balerdi’s swipe at fresh air deep inside his own box gifted Cunha the simplest task to tap in an equaliser seven minutes from time. Three minutes later, the Brazilian thundered a shot past Vasquez at his near post and flung himself into the crowd in what proved to be a costly celebration. Cunha was booked and then shown a second yellow card moments later for a wild lunge in stoppage time. The 10 men held on to breathe new life into United’s Champions League campaign after back-to-back defeats against Atletico Madrid and Como. Whether it proves to be a turning point or just another stay of execution for Carrick remains to be seen. items.title: Calendrier électoral 2026 : Le corps électoral officiellement convoqué pour les régionales et les sénatoriales
items.description: Le compte à rebours est lancé pour les prochaines échéances électorales locales et nationales. À travers un décret officiel lu sur les antennes par le général Amara Camara, porte-parole de la Présidence de la République, le chef de l'État a fixé les dates clés pour le renouvellement des instances régionales et de la haute chambre parlementaire. ​Conformément à la Constitution, au code électoral (loi organique L/2025/026/CNT) ainsi qu'à l'avis de la Cour suprême, les citoyens et collèges concernés devront se rendre aux urnes à deux reprises avant la fin de l'année : ​ Élections régionales : Le corps électoral est convoqué le dimanche 29 novembre 2026 sur l'ensemble du territoire national pour élire les conseillers régionaux. Ce scrutin mobilisera un collège électoral formé par les conseillers communaux. Le nombre d'électeurs inscrits pour cette élection est arrêté à 8 783. ​ Élections sénatoriales : Prévues pour le dimanche 20 décembre 2026, elles permettront d'élire les deux tiers des sénateurs. Le collège électoral sera cette fois-ci composé des conseillers régionaux et des conseillers communaux. Le fichier électoral pour ce scrutin dénombre 8 780 électeurs inscrits. ​L'application stricte de ce décret a été confiée aux membres du gouvernement concernés. Sont notamment impliqués la ministre de l'Administration du territoire et de la Décentralisation, le ministre de la Justice et des Droits de l'Homme, le ministre de la Sécurité et de la Protection civile, le ministre délégué à la Défense nationale, ainsi que le ministre de l'Économie, des Finances et du Budget. Les autres services et institutions compétents en matière électorale devront également veiller à la bonne tenue de ces opérations sur l'ensemble du pays.

items.title: Atiku’s claim: DSS denies plotting Sokoto protest, orders probe
items.description: The Department of State Services (DSS) has denied allegations that it planned to organise protests in Sokoto State, describing the claim by former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as inconsistent with its operations. The Service, however, said its Director-General had ordered an investigation into the allegation in deference to the former vice president. In a statement issued on Tuesday by the Deputy Director, Public Relations and Strategic Communications, Favour Dozie, the DSS said its operatives deployed to protect the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Mannir Daniya, evacuated him to safety when he was attacked on October 31, 2026. According to the Service, Daniya escaped unhurt during the incident, while two DSS operatives were assaulted and were still receiving treatment in hospital as of the time of the statement. The DSS said the governorship candidate personally contacted the State Director of the Service in Sokoto to express appreciation for the intervention and subsequently requested additional security reinforcement. The Service also cited its arrest and prosecution of Monday Udeme Steven in Rivers State on March 2, 2026, for allegedly threatening to attack the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi. It said Steven was prosecuted before a Federal High Court in Rivers State and sentenced to two years’ imprisonment. The DSS said its operations to protect politicians across party lines contradicted Atiku’s allegation, which it argued could demoralise its operatives risking their lives in the line of duty. Read Also: Atiku accuses DSS of plotting to disrupt ADC rally in Sokoto It nevertheless said the Director-General had ordered an investigation into the allegation out of respect for the former vice president. The Service also recalled a similar allegation by African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, that it was involved in an attack on him in Ekiti State. It said it appreciated the police for their swift investigation and preliminary report on the incident, which identified an altercation as its cause and led to the arrest of 11 suspects. The DSS added that it would await the outcome of the police investigation and would not dissipate further energy on the matter. The Service reaffirmed its commitment to accountability under its current Director-General. The post Atiku’s claim: DSS denies plotting Sokoto protest, orders probe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Restructuration et départ à la retraite : Vague importante de départs d’officiers au sein de l’Armée et de la Gendarmerie
items.description: Dans le cadre de la réorganisation des effectifs et de l'application de la réglementation militaire en vigueur, un décret présidentiel fixant la mise à la retraite d'un nombre important d'officiers et sous-officiers des Forces Armées Guinéennes a été rendu public ce mardi 3 novembre 2026. ​Cette décision administrative majeure concerne l'Armée de Terre, l’Armée de Mer ainsi que la Gendarmerie Nationale, touchant plusieurs hauts gradés arrivés au terme de leur carrière militaire. ​Le décret s'articule autour de deux critères juridiques d'admission à la retraite, notamment la limite d'âge révolue. Elle concerne plusieurs dizaines d'officiers généraux, supérieurs et subalternes admis à faire valoir leurs droits à la retraite. Parmi eux figure le Général de brigade Michel Ange Bangoura (65 ans), aux côtés de nombreux colonels et lieutenants-colonels (âgés de 63 ans), capitaines (58 ans), lieutenants (56 ans) et sous-officiers. ​Quant au deuxième critère, il s'appuie sur la limite de la durée de service. Le décret met également à la retraite une série d'officiers de l'Armée de Terre ayant accompli la durée maximale légale de service actif, fixée à 40 ans de loyaux services sous le drapeau. C'est un total de 111 personnes (militaires et gendarmes) qui sont concernées au total par cette mise à la retraite, réparties de la manière suivante : Pour limite d'âge : 53 personnes (comprenant l'Armée de terre, l'Armée de mer et la Gendarmerie nationale). Pour limite de durée de service : 58 personnes (appartenant à l'Armée de terre, l'Armée de mer et la Gendarmerie nationale). Nous reviendrons sur leur liste intégrale !

items.title: Lekjaa exclut un retour des carburants à la compensation
items.description: Lors de l’examen détaillé du PLF 2027 en commission des Finances de la Chambre des représentants, Fouzi Lekjaa a fermé la porte à tout retour des carburants dans la Caisse de compensation, un soutien généralisé qu’il juge coûteux et peu équitable. Le ministre a aussi défendu les marges des distributeurs, plaidé pour la séparation des activités d’importation et de distribution, et évoqué l’avenir de la SAMIR. Le ministre de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Performance publique, Fouzi Lekjaa, écarte toute possibilité de réintégrer les produits pétroliers dans le système de compensation. Il assure que l'Exécutif suit au quotidien, de près, l'évolution des prix des matières premières et des intrants de l'économie nationale en provenance des marchés internationaux. Lors de la réunion de la commission des Finances et du Développement économique de la Chambre des représentants, consacrée ce mardi à la discussion détaillée du projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027, Lekjaa a plaidé pour un langage de vérité envers les citoyens, loin de toute « démagogie ». Il a réaffirmé que le rétablissement d'un soutien via la Caisse de compensation n'est pas à l'ordre du jour. Pour le ministre, le mécanisme traditionnel de compensation profite surtout aux catégories au pouvoir d'achat élevé et aux plus gros consommateurs, tandis que les ménages vulnérables et pauvres en bénéficient le moins. Il a souligné que mobiliser des enveloppes considérables, pouvant atteindre entre 50 et 70 milliards de dirhams par an, dans un soutien généralisé et non ciblé, « ne permettrait pas d'atteindre la justice sociale et ne protégerait pas, en premier lieu, les couches visées ». Alors que des propositions de baisse des droits et taxes appliqués aux carburants étaient débattues, le ministre a averti que la suppression de la taxe intérieure de consommation (TIC) ne ferait baisser le prix que d'environ 1,20 dirham par litre. Sur la polémique relative aux bénéfices des sociétés de distribution de carburants, Lekjaa a présenté les indicateurs financiers du secteur. Le chiffre d'affaires des opérateurs est passé à 131 milliards de dirhams en 2025, avec une marge bénéficiaire d'environ 5,85 %, à comparer au pic de rentabilité enregistré en 2017. Selon lui, ces chiffres doivent être appréciés en les comparant à ceux des autres secteurs commerciaux, et en tenant compte des risques liés à l'importation et de la volatilité des cours sur le marché de Rotterdam, qui oblige les sociétés à programmer leurs commandes et leurs stocks jusqu'à trois mois à l'avance. Au chapitre des réformes structurelles, le ministre a fixé les priorités de la période : parachever les conditions d'une concurrence libre, accroître les capacités de stockage nationales pour renforcer la sécurité énergétique, et traiter la question du lien actuel entre les activités d'importation et de distribution, en allant vers leur séparation afin de limiter d'éventuels dysfonctionnements et de garantir une transparence totale sur le marché intérieur. Abordant le dossier de la raffinerie SAMIR, Lekjaa a estimé que le sujet appelle un examen objectif, sans simplification excessive : le raffinage n'est plus un choix stratégique, même pour les grands pays producteurs, et il ne garantit pas nécessairement une baisse des prix à l'échelle locale, surtout lorsque le baril dépasse la barre des 100 dollars. Il s'est en revanche dit favorable à toute initiative de partenariat public-privé ou à tout investissement, marocain ou étranger, qui contribuerait à remettre l'installation en service, précisant que la valeur réelle de la raffinerie réside aujourd'hui avant tout dans ses infrastructures, qui peuvent renforcer le stock stratégique du Royaume. The post Lekjaa exclut un retour des carburants à la compensation appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
