items.title: PI-SPI : la révolution silencieuse des paiements dans l’UEMOA ( par Maître Amadou SOW)
items.description: Pendant longtemps, envoyer de l’argent en Afrique de l’Ouest impliquait soit le transport d’espèces, soit des virements bancaires dont l’exécution pouvait nécessiter plusieurs jours. L’essor du Mobile Money a ensuite profondément modifié les habitudes des populations en permettant des envois rapides à partir d’un simple téléphone portable. Cette pratique s’est tellement développée que dans le langage courant l’envoi Mobile Money est assimilé au son émis par les smartphones à la réception, « Ting » pour ironiser la réception des montants tant attendus. Toutefois, cette évolution a rapidement révélé une limite importante : les banques, opérateurs de monnaie électronique et autres prestataires de services financiers fonctionnaient souvent dans des systèmes différents qui communiquaient difficilement entre eux ou pas du tout. Pour remédier à ce cloisonnement( parfois exprès selon la logique du marché) la Banque Centrale des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (BCEAO), institution chargée notamment de la politique monétaire et de la supervision des systèmes de paiement au sein de l’Union Économique et Monétaire Ouest-Africaine (UEMOA), regroupant le Bénin, le Burkina Faso, la Côte d’Ivoire, la Guinée-Bissau, le Mali, le Niger, le Sénégal et le Togo, a lancé le 30 septembre 2025 la Plateforme Interopérable du Système de Paiement Instantané (PI-SPI). Une infrastructure commune, et non une application Contrairement à une idée largement répandue, PI-SPI n’est pas une application mobile que l’on télécharge sur son téléphone (pour ceux qui ont eu le réflexe du téléchargement, ne pas se décourager). Il s’agit d’une infrastructure régionale de paiement conçue et opérée par la BCEAO. Les utilisateurs continuent donc d’utiliser leurs applications habituelles, qu’il s’agisse d’applications mobil Money ou de leurs applications bancaire ou d’autres services financiers numériques. L’innovation repose sur le principe de l’interopérabilité, c’est-à-dire la capacité de systèmes différents à communiquer et à fonctionner ensemble. Cela signifie qu’un utilisateur peut envoyer ou recevoir de l’argent entre différentes banques, différents opérateurs de monnaie électronique ou institutions financières, sans être limité par le réseau utilisé par son correspondant. Grâce à PI-SPI, un titulaire de compte bancaire peut envoyer directement de l’argent à un utilisateur de portefeuille électronique, tandis qu’un utilisateur de Mobile Money peut recevoir des fonds provenant d’une banque différente. Les transactions sont exécutées en quelques secondes, vingt-quatre heures sur vingt-quatre et sept jours sur sept (Las de suivre l’exécution d’un virement). Un projet soutenu par un cadre réglementaire ambitieux Après une phase de tests en conditions réelles lancée en 2025, la BCEAO a progressivement organisé le raccordement de l’ensemble des acteurs financiers de l’Union à cette infrastructure régionale. Ainsi, les banques, les établissements de monnaie électronique, les établissements de paiement ainsi que les institutions de microfinance de l’UEMOA ont été invités à achever leur connexion à PI-SPI selon un calendrier fixé par la Banque Centrale. L’objectif était d’assurer une interopérabilité effective entre tous les participants, afin que chaque utilisateur puisse effectuer des transactions avec n’importe quel établissement raccordé à la plateforme. Une nouvelle étape a été franchie avec l’Avis n°0019 du 2 octobre 2026 relatif aux transactions de monnaie électronique entre personnes physiques par l’intermédiaire de la Plateforme Interopérable du Système de Paiement Instantané (PI-SPI) de l’UEMOA. Ce texte prévoit expressément que : « Toutes les transactions de monnaie électronique interopérables, au sein de l’UEMOA, sont obligatoirement réalisées par l’intermédiaire de PI-SPI ». PI-SPI est ainsi passé du statut de nouvelle infrastructure de paiement à celui de plateforme de référence pour les transactions interopérables au sein de l’Union. Une tarification conçue pour favoriser les petits transferts L’un des apports majeurs de l’Avis n°0019 réside dans l’encadrement des frais applicables aux transferts entre particuliers. La BCEAO a souhaité favoriser les opérations du quotidien tout en limitant les coûts supportés par les usagers. Les règles sont relativement simples : les transferts nationaux dont le montant cumulé quotidien est inférieur ou égal à 8 000 FCFA sont gratuits ; au-delà de ce seuil, des frais peuvent être appliqués ; ces frais sont plafonnés à 0,8 % du montant du transfert hors taxes ; la réception des fonds demeure gratuite. Il convient toutefois de souligner que le seuil de gratuité s’apprécie sur le montant total des transferts réalisés au cours d’une même journée et non opération par opération. Prenons un exemple simple. Une utilisatrice effectue dans la journée trois transferts de 2 000 FCFA, 3 000 FCFA et 2 500 FCFA. Le montant total transféré est de 7 500 FCFA. Ce montant restant inférieur au seuil de 8 000 FCFA, l’ensemble des opérations demeure gratuit. En revanche, si un utilisateur transfère 5 000 FCFA le matin puis 6 000 FCFA l’après-midi, le montant cumulé atteint 11 000 FCFA. Le seuil étant dépassé, l’établissement financier concerné pourra appliquer des frais dans la limite du plafond réglementaire fixé par la BCEAO. À titre d’illustration, un transfert de 10 000 FCFA soumis au taux maximal autorisé ne pourrait générer plus de 80 FCFA de frais hors taxes. Comment utiliser PI-SPI concrètement ? L’utilisation de PI-SPI ne nécessite aucune inscription particulière ni téléchargement spécifique. Il suffit que la banque ou le service de monnaie électronique utilisé soit connecté à la plateforme. Un utilisateur peut notamment : envoyer de l’argent depuis un compte bancaire vers un portefeuille électronique ; transférer des fonds d’un portefeuille électronique vers un compte bancaire ; réaliser des transferts entre opérateurs différents ; payer un commerçant à l’aide d’un QR Code compatible ; recevoir instantanément des fonds provenant d’un autre établissement financier. Ainsi, un client OM peut désormais transférer des fonds à un utilisateur d’un autre réseau participant à PI-SPI sans avoir à se préoccuper de l’opérateur utilisé par ce dernier. De la même manière, une entreprise peut régler un fournisseur ou un salarié sur un compte relevant d’un établissement différent sans subir les contraintes techniques qui existaient auparavant. Au-delà de l’innovation technologique, PI-SPI constitue un instrument d’intégration économique régionale. En créant une infrastructure unique reliant les banques, les établissements de monnaie électronique, les établissements de paiement et les institutions de microfinance de l’UEMOA, la BCEAO poursuit un objectif clair : rendre les paiements plus rapides, plus accessibles et moins coûteux pour les citoyens et les entreprises. Après avoir connu la révolution du Mobile Money, l’Afrique de l’Ouest entre ainsi dans une nouvelle phase de modernisation des paiements, fondée sur l’interopérabilité, la célérité et l’intégration régionale. Les frontières techniques entre opérateurs tendent progressivement à disparaître au profit d’un écosystème unifié où l’argent circule librement entre les différents acteurs du système financier. Dans notre prochain article, nous reviendrons plus en détail sur le cadre réglementaire ayant accompagné le déploiement de cette infrastructure, notamment la décision de raccordement obligatoire à la plateforme PI-SPI ainsi que les mesures de prolongation des délais de connexion imposées aux banques, établissements de monnaie électronique, établissements de paiement et institutions de microfinance de l’UEMOA. Maître Amadou SOW Avocat-Conseil Formalis Lawyers Tous droits réservés Dakar, octobre 2026

items.title: Ligue des champions: Paris en démonstration, Manchester United renversant
items.description: Toujours aussi impressionnant, le PSG a encore frappé fort en écrasant Villarreal mardi lors de la 4e journée de Ligue des champions, où Manchester United s'est offert un peu d'air grâce à un succès renversant contre la Roma. Moins de huit minutes pour tuer une rencontre: avec quatre buts de quatre joueurs différents entre la 9e et la 17e minute (Joao Neves, Désiré Doué, Mayulu puis Fabian Ruiz), le PSG a mis KO Villarreal, finalement surclassé 6-0 dans son stade de la Céramique. Déjà sortis vainqueurs de leurs chocs contre Manchester City et Barcelone, les doubles tenants du titre parisiens ont fait le spectacle malgré leurs absents (Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos, Mendes…). Ils sont plus que jamais seuls en tête de la phase de ligue avec 12 points sur 12 possibles et une avalanche de buts marqués, avant de recevoir la Roma fin novembre. La Louve a elle bien cru jouer un mauvais tour à Manchester United à Old Trafford: menés 2-0, les Red Devils se sont finalement imposés 3-2 dans un stade en fusion, et repoussent la crise. Grâce notamment à un doublé de Matheus Cunha (83e, 86e), parti célébrer au milieu de ses supporters, les Mancuniens ont mis fin à une série de neuf matches sans victoire toutes compétitions confondues, une situation inédite depuis 1984. Ce succès renversant va peut-être offrir un sursis à leur entraîneur Michael Carrick, encore fragilisé par le revers contre Chelsea samedi mais soutenu une nouvelle fois par son public mardi. – Le Barça redémarre – Sous un déluge au Camp Nou, Barcelone a décroché un beau succès face à Aston Villa (3-0), qui comptait jusqu'ici trois victoires en autant de journées. Dominés par le PSG (4-2) puis par le Real lors du Classico (2-1), les Blaugranas se rassurent, deuxièmes avec neuf points. Les Catalans ont d'abord profité d'une erreur de relance des Villans, offrant un cadeau que Lamine Yamal s'est chargé de propulser dans les filets d'un bel enroulé du gauche (7e). Raphinha (52e, 64e) a alourdi la marque. L'affiche de la soirée entre l'Atlético Madrid et le Bayern Munich a elle profité aux Bavarois (2-0), qui restaient sur deux nuls. Si le Ballon d'Or Harry Kane a été muet, le jeune Lennart Karl, 18 ans, a profité d'une perte de balle de Robin Le Normand dans sa surface pour faire sauter le verrou des Colchoneros (54e), trop timides offensivement pour renverser la partie, dont Konrad Laimer a scellé l'issue d'une frappe surpuissante (74e). Plombé par deux défaites consécutives face au Real et Bruges pour entamer sa campagne européenne, l'Inter a confirmé son redressement avec une nette victoire à Rotterdam contre le Feyenoord (3-0). Les Interistes affichent le même bilan (6 points) et la même dynamique (deux défaites puis deux victoires) que Galatasaray, qui a dominé Stuttgart 2-0 grâce à un doublé du jeune milieu russe Alexeï Batrakov. Le Sporting Portugal, quart de finaliste l'an passé et qui devrait bientôt voir arriver à sa tête l'ex-entraîneur de Lyon Paulo Fonseca, a lui battu sans briller le Chakhtar Donetsk à Londres (1-0) et pointe dans le Top 8 avec 9 points. Déjà sous pression avec trois revers, Lille n'a pu faire mieux qu'un triste nul 0-0 sur la pelouse synthétique de Bodoe/Glimt, en Norvège au nord du cercle polaire. De quoi débloquer son compteur, mais insuffisant pour viser une qualification. items.title: Sánchez reivindica la dimisión de Puente tras “dar la cara”: “Demuestra que no todos somos iguales”
items.description: Nadie lo sabía. Ni el mismísimo Pedro Sánchez. Óscar Puente ocultó al presidente del Gobierno su dimisión como ministro de Transportes hasta unos minutos antes de que la anunciara justo al final de su comparecencia en el Congreso para dar explicaciones por el accidente ferroviario de Urda. “Ha dado la cara, ha dado soluciones y, después, ha dado un paso al lado”, ha valorado Sánchez en un mensaje emotivo en redes sociales. El presidente ha destacado que la salida de Puente del Ejecutivo se produce “por dignidad” y “voluntad propia”. En definitiva, “por respeto a las víctimas y al proyecto progresista”. La conclusión de Sánchez es que el ejemplo de Puente “dignifica” a España “y demuestra que no todos somos iguales”. “Mientras unos solo dan lecciones, otros lo dan todo”, ha enfatizado en una andanada al PP. items.title: Why a US-Russia showdown left Morocco celebrating
items.description: Morocco has welcomed the end of a decades-long UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, after a diplomatic showdown between the US and Russia left the Security Council unable to agree on its future. The council failed on Friday to renew the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (Minurso) after Russia vetoed a US-backed proposal. A rival Russian draft to extend the mission also failed to secure enough votes. The decision raises questions about the future of Africa’s longest territorial dispute and the fragile ceasefire between Morocco, which claims Western Sahara, and the Polisario Front, which has been fighting for the territory’s independence for more than 50 years. Here is what you need to know. Why is Western Sahara disputed? Western Sahara, on Africa’s northwest coast, was a Spanish colony until 1975. It has significant phosphate reserves and valuable fishing grounds along its Atlantic coast. As Spain prepared to withdraw, both Morocco and Mauritania claimed the territory. The International Court of Justice found historical ties of allegiance but no territorial sovereignty that overrode the Sahrawi people’s right to self-determination. Morocco’s then King Hassan II responded by organising the Green March. On 6 November 1975, about 350,000 Moroccan civilians entered the territory in a mass demonstration intended to put pressure on Spain. Days later, Spain signed the Madrid Accords with Morocco and Mauritania, agreeing to transfer administrative control. Morocco took the northern two-thirds and Mauritania the southern third. The agreement did not settle the sovereignty question. The Polisario Front, an independence movement founded in 1973, opposed the deal. It saw it as replacing Spanish colonial rule with Moroccan and Mauritanian control. Mauritania renounced its claim in 1979, but Morocco continued fighting Polisario. Algeria became Polisario’s main regional ally, providing military support and hosting its leadership and thousands of Sahrawi refugees in camps near the city of Tindouf. The North African country says its position is based on the right to self-determination, while Morocco sees Western Sahara as an integral part of its territory. Morocco and Algeria fought a brief border war in 1963 over disagreements about territory inherited from French colonial rule. Their relationship has remained tense, with Western Sahara at the centre of their dispute. What was the UN’s mission role? After 16 years of fighting, Morocco and Polisario agreed to a UN-brokered ceasefire in 1991, with a sand wall, or berm, dividing the territory to keep the rival forces apart. The UN established Minurso to monitor the ceasefire and organise a referendum on the territory’s future. Sahrawis were meant to choose between independence and integration with Morocco. The vote was scheduled for 1992 but never took place. The two sides could not agree on who was eligible to participate, and disputes over voter identification became a major obstacle. In 2007, Morocco proposed autonomy, which would let Sahrawis manage their internal affairs while Rabat retained control over defence and foreign relations. Thousands of Moroccans marched into Western Sahara in 1975 in what became known as the Green March The Polisario Front and Algeria rejected the plan, insisting on a referendum that included independence as an option. Years of UN-sponsored negotiations failed to produce a breakthrough. The ceasefire broke down in November 2020, when Polisario said it was resuming armed struggle. But after a long diplomatic campaign by Morocco, the UN Security Council voted in 2025 to back the autonomy plan as the “most feasible” solution for the disputed territory. While most Sahrawis live in the part of Western Sahara controlled by Morocco, tens of thousands are estimated to be in refugee camps in Algeria. What happened at the UN? The US proposed extending Minurso’s mandate for another year, but its draft went beyond the usual renewal. It would have removed the word “referendum” from the mission’s name and made Morocco’s autonomy proposal the sole basis for further negotiations. The draft received the support of 11 of the Security Council’s 15 members, including France and the UK but Russia vetoed it, arguing that it was too favourable to Morocco. Russia then proposed extending Minurso’s mandate without changing its terms. That draft also failed, receiving only two votes in favour. Minurso’s mandate expired at the end of Saturday, 31 October. The UN said the following day that the mission had entered a liquidation period, with a reduced team overseeing the transfer of military equipment and other assets. The UN mission has been in Western Sahara since 1991 UN Secretary-General António Guterres said the Sahrawi people’s right to self-determination must be respected and warned of the risk of renewed hostilities. The Polisario Front condemned the US proposal. Its representative, Sidi Omar, thanked Russia for vetoing it, saying it would “torpedo the foundations of the UN peace process” and threaten regional and international peace. Morocco, meanwhile, said the mission’s personnel and equipment should leave the territory in the coming days, arguing that the Security Council should no longer consider the Western Sahara issue. Minurso had 155 military personnel and was expected to cost $62m (£46m) in the financial year beginning in June, according to a UN report. Why is Morocco celebrating the end of the UN mission? Morocco’s royal palace welcomed the failure to renew Minurso’s mandate. In Laayoune, the territory’s largest city, footage showed people celebrating, waving Moroccan flags and displaying portraits of King Mohammed VI. “The decision is an opportunity for Rabat to challenge what it sees as an international mechanism that has failed to resolve the dispute,” Issam Laaroussi, a Moroccan expert in international relations, tells the BBC. He said Morocco now has more room to push its autonomy proposal and shift negotiations away from a referendum on independence toward autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty. The decision does not, however, change Western Sahara’s legal status or amount to international recognition of Moroccan sovereignty. Western Sahara remains on the UN list of non-self-governing territories, while the African Union officially recognises its independence, as the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR). But the decision comes after several countries backed Morocco’s position, which in recent years has made securing international support for its claim central to its foreign policy. In 2020, the US recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara as part of an agreement to establish diplomatic relations between Morocco and Israel.In 2024, France also backed Morocco’s autonomy plan as the basis for resolving the dispute. Thousands of Sahrawis live in refugee camps in Algeria Morocco rejoined the African Union in 2017, more than three decades after leaving its predecessor, the Organisation of African Unity, in protest at the SADR’s admission. Since returning, Rabat has sought to build support for its position from within the organisation. At least 10 African countries have opened diplomatic missions in the territory in support of Rabat. “Morocco is not necessarily seeking to abandon the UN process, but to change the framework for negotiations and draw greater support from regional organisations,” says Laaroussi. Addressing a special joint session of parliament on Monday, House of Representatives Speaker Ahmed Touizi hailed the end of Minurso as a victory for the country’s diplomacy. He said the country should now move from “managing the dispute to implementing its autonomy plan under Moroccan sovereignty, while pressing ahead with development projects in the territory.” Could this lead to a renewed war? The fear is that Minurso’s departure could lead to renewed fighting. The mission has monitored military developments and helped reduce the risk of escalation. Aid organisation Oxfam warned that losing its monitoring and de-escalation role could undermine stability, with serious consequences for civilians. Laaroussi admits that the mission’s departure could create security gaps. “Minurso’s departure does not create the original conflict, because the conflict is already there, but it could aggravate an already fragile security environment,” he says. The UN decision has also fuelled nationalist rhetoric online. Several Moroccan users have shared AI-generated images of themselves in military uniform, declaring their readiness to fight for Morocco’s sovereignty over Western Sahara. In Morocco, Western Sahara is widely regarded as a national cause. Political parties that are often divided on other issues are united in supporting the country’s claim to sovereignty over the territory. Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita has said the end of the mission does not mean the end of the ceasefire, and that Rabat remains committed to it “within respect of its security and sovereignty.” Polisario has not said what it will do next. Any resumption of fighting could well draw in Algeria, as tensions with Morocco remain high. According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), both countries significantly increased military spending last year, with SIPRI citing their dispute over Western Sahara as a key driver. Algeria spent an estimated $25.4bn, more than four time Morocco’s $6.3bn.

items.title: Libya’s top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes
items.description: Libya’s highest religious authority, the Dar al-Ifta, has issued a ruling banning Muslims from buying, selling or wearing clothing bearing the Nike logo. The ruling, issued by the Tripoli-based institution, states that the US sportswear giant was named after the Greek goddess of victory and that its famous swoosh logo was inspired by her wings. It argued that wearing clothing displaying the logo amounted to promoting symbols associated “with polytheism,” or the worship of more than one god. Libya is home to the ancient Greek city of Cyrene, where archaeological remains include a statue of the Greek goddess of the same name. The religious committee also accused Nike of supporting Israel and called for a boycott of companies that back the country. It referred to a statement issued by its Council for Research and Sharia Studies on 5 November 2023, urging Muslims to boycott Western companies it considers supportive of Israel during the war in Gaza. The ruling, known as a fatwa, is a religious opinion on a matter of Islamic law. Libya’s Grand Mufti, Sadiq al-Gharyani, approved it. The BBC has contacted Nike for comment. The Dar al-Ifta is an influential religious institution based in Tripoli, in western Libya. The country is politically divided, with rival authorities and institutions operating in the east and west after years of conflict following the toppling of long-time leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011. Although its religious rulings can carry considerable social influence, they are not necessarily government orders or legally enforceable. Last year it ruled against wearing jewellery and watches bearing the logo of French luxury jewellery house Van Cleef & Arpels, arguing that its four-leaf clover design was associated with Christian beliefs and the pursuit of good luck, which it said contradicted Islamic teachings. The latest fatwa does not announce a state ban on Nike products or specify penalties for people who continue to buy or wear them. Social media reactions were mixed, with some users welcoming the ruling while others questioned its significance, calling it ironic or a distraction from more pressing issues. The ruling comes amid wider debates over the rise of religious conservatism in public life in Libya. In 2025, authorities in eastern Libya announced restrictions on rap music, theatre and dance performances, citing concerns that some lyrics and performances violated public morals and Islamic values. Authorities later extended the measures to western Libya. The Dar al-Ifta has also previously issued religious rulings against music, although there is no clear evidence that it was directly involved in the restrictions on performances. Nike does not operate an official store in Libya; however, local sportswear retailers carry Nike-branded products. Sportswear brands such as Nike and Adidas are popular across North Africa. In Libya, as in other countries in the region, local markets also sell counterfeit versions of popular sportswear brands.

items.title: 2027: Ogun indigenes rally behind Adebutu, reaffirm ‘Ogun for Ogun’ agenda
items.description: .pledge grassroots mobilisation as PDP candidate takes campaign to communities By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Indigenes of Ogun State have reaffirmed their commitment to protecting the state’s political heritage, declaring support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ movement ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The residents made the pledge during separate engagements at the ward-to-ward campaign tours of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, and his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, across the state’s local government areas. The campaign tour, which has taken Adebutu and Kolapo to various communities in recent weeks, is aimed at mobilising grassroots support for the PDP candidates and presenting their seven-point development agenda, tagged ITURA DE, to the electorate. At the different ward meetings, residents, community leaders, market women, farmers and youths turned out to welcome the candidates, with several communities receiving them with colourful displays and enthusiastic celebrations. The engagements also provided opportunities for residents to interact directly with the candidates, raise concerns about their communities and outline their expectations from the next administration. Among the major issues raised were the poor condition of rural roads, unemployment, inadequate agricultural support and the need for improved infrastructure and access to modern farming equipment. Several stakeholders pledged to mobilise support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ initiative, arguing that the state’s leadership should reflect the interests, heritage and aspirations of its indigenes. At Alagada Ward in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area, a market leader, Mrs Folasade Ogunye, said her support for the movement was informed by the belief that indigenous leadership would better understand the challenges confronting grassroots communities. She lamented the poor condition of roads leading to markets and the limited employment opportunities available to young people, insisting that residents needed a leader who understood their everyday struggles. “We, the women of Obafemi/Owode, have suffered neglect. Our roads to the markets are bad, and our children need jobs. We want someone who grew up here, who knows our language and understands our struggles. “We believe that someone with a genuine connection to the people will better appreciate our challenges. That is why we have pledged to go from house to house to mobilise support for this mandate. It is about our pride and the future of Ogun indigenes,” she said. In a related development, some residents said to be former members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) at Alapakooni community in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area publicly renounced their allegiance to the party. The defectors reportedly set bunches of APC brooms ablaze to symbolise their departure from the party, citing dissatisfaction with its political leadership and questions surrounding the identity of its governorship candidate. A community youth coordinator in Alapakooni Ward, Tunde Akinola, said their decision to align with Adebutu was motivated by their desire for leadership they could identify with and hold accountable. “We decided to join this ward meeting today with our incoming governor, Adebutu, because we love our state and cannot trade its future on the altar of politics. “We want to follow someone we know, someone who understands our people and has the capacity to deliver on his promises,” Akinola said. Similarly, a community stakeholder and farmer at Onidunu Ward, Deji Bamidele, said farmers in the area were eager for a government that would prioritise agricultural development through mechanisation and improved access to farming inputs. He lamented that many farmers still depended on rudimentary implements despite the increasing need to boost food production. “In this community, farming is our life, but we have been left with cutlasses while farmers in other states are benefiting from tractors and modern equipment. “When Adebutu explained the ITURA DE agenda and how agriculture would be mechanised, we saw hope. We are committing our farmers’ cooperative, which has more than 300 members, to the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ cause because we want our agricultural potential properly harnessed,” he said. At Owode Ward 3, also in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area, a retired teacher, Alhaja Sariyu Bankole, described the movement as an opportunity to preserve the state’s political heritage. According to her, Ogun State has produced several distinguished leaders whose legacies should inspire the emergence of leadership that understands the history and aspirations of its people. “We cannot mortgage our heritage. Ogun State is the home of great leaders, and we must ensure that whoever governs us understands our history and respects the people. “I have spoken to my former students and their parents in this ward about the need to participate actively in the election. We must make our voices count and work towards the future we desire,” she said. In Sagamu Local Government Area, a youth leader, Comrade Bayo Oduwole, said young people were determined to play a more active role in determining the political future of the state. Speaking at Ward 10, Oduwole maintained that the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ campaign should be driven by competence, accountability and a genuine understanding of the state’s needs. “The courageous indigenes of this state have called on us not to surrender our future, and we agree with the need for leadership that understands our people and their aspirations. “We know Adebutu’s family history here and are familiar with the contributions associated with his family. We also recognise the compassion shown by Iya Sunnah. We will mobilise our youths through voter education and door-to-door campaigns to secure victory,” he said. Responding to the expressions of support, Adebutu described the ward-to-ward engagements as an opportunity to understand the needs of communities and build a development agenda around them. He said the ITURA DE agenda was designed to address the socio-economic challenges facing the state, with particular attention to infrastructure, agriculture, employment generation and improved living standards. “This tour has shown me that our people are yearning for homegrown leadership that understands their challenges and is prepared to address them. “The ITURA DE agenda is not just a slogan; it is a social contract to restore dignity, fix our roads, empower our farmers, create jobs for our youths and return Ogun State to its rightful place. “We are not just campaigning; we are listening to the people, understanding their concerns and taking note of their expectations. We will deliver on our promises,” Adebutu said. Also speaking, the PDP deputy governorship candidate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, assured residents that a government led by the party would prioritise inclusive governance and ensure that grassroots communities were adequately represented in policy decisions. She particularly highlighted the importance of women, children, education and primary healthcare in the proposed administration’s development plans. “What we have witnessed in the wards we have visited is genuine concern and love for Ogun State. The people want a government that listens to them and responds to their needs. “As a mother and a daughter of this soil, I assure you that our government will prioritise women, children, education and primary healthcare. “We will not disappoint the people. This ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate is about building a state where every community, irrespective of its location or social standing, has a sense of belonging and benefits from good governance,” Kolapo said. The PDP candidates maintained that their ongoing grassroots engagements would continue across the state as they seek to consolidate support and present their policy proposals ahead of the 2027 governorship election. items.title: Trump Repeats a Centuries-Old Mistake
items.description: This is a special Election Day edition of Time-Travel Thursdays, a journey through The Atlantic ’s archives to contextualize the present. Sign up here. “The President of the United States has so singular a combination of defects for the office of a constitutional magistrate, that he could have obtained the opportunity to misrule the nation only by a visitation of Providence.” So begins one of the most withering paragraphs on politics in the history of The Atlantic . “He unites in his character the seemingly opposite qualities of demagogue and autocrat,” the passage continues, “and converts the Presidential chair into a stump or a throne, according as the impulse seizes him to cajole or to command.” These words, written by E. P. Whipple , date back to September 1866, in the midst of a midterm election battle. The sitting president, Andrew Johnson, had been thrust into office a little more than a year earlier by John Wilkes Booth. By the time Whipple’s essay appeared, Johnson had placed himself at the center of a congressional election that would have defining consequences for the country. With the guns of the Civil War still warm, the fundamental questions of Reconstruction were at the core of national politics. The Republican majority in Congress insisted that Reconstruction must do more than simply restore Confederate states to the Union: It must secure the rights of formerly enslaved people and prevent certain former Confederate leaders from returning to political power. Johnson, a War Democrat from Tennessee who’d been nominated to balance Abraham Lincoln’s National Union ticket in 1864, took another view. Whipple’s essays on the theatrics of Johnson’s campaign are the work of a writer at the height of his powers, but who also may be losing his mind. Whipple performed surgical eviscerations of Johnson and his allies’ efforts to nullify the Union triumph in the Civil War. Nearly blinded by his racism and opposition to Black civil rights, Johnson set himself at odds with the Republican majority, pardoning thousands of former Confederates, vetoing Reconstruction legislation, and excusing white violence on Black Americans in Memphis and New Orleans. In his essays, Whipple confronted the maddening diversions of what he called the “Johnson Party,” in which secessionists were portrayed as the true patriots, presidential overreach and usurpation were said to be in service of the Constitution, and those opposing both were seen as the real traitors. “There is no wrong anywhere,” Whipple lamented. “It is all ‘right.’” Whipple’s shouts resonate in our own up-is-down era of politics, and in a midterm cycle in which Donald Trump, like Johnson in 1866, “sees hardly anything as it is, but almost everything as colored by his own dominant egotism.” Trump’s attempt to hold on to his party’s majority has focused on defending his record and deflecting questions about affordability and high gas prices. Some Republican candidates are distancing themselves from him ahead of Election Day, as his appearances veer into unusual tangents removed from voters’ everyday concerns (for good measure, he recently took to praising the “ass” of Senator Jon Husted of Ohio and the rapper Nicki Minaj ). Johnson, too, defined the election as a referendum not just on the nation and its future, but on his destiny in shaping it. With whispers of a possible impeachment dogging him that year, the midterms represented a showdown between the executive and legislative branches. Whipple’s essay on “The Johnson Party” came after the so-called National Union Convention, an August 1866 event that Johnson and his Cabinet had endorsed to form a new coalition that could displace the pro-Reconstruction Republican majority in Congress. In the case that Johnson’s new party failed to win, some of his supporters reportedly discussed schemes to deny Republicans power. If “Congress cannot be overcome by fair means, it will be by foul,” Whipple wrote. “In short, we are promised, on the assembling of the next Congress, a coup d’état .” To rally support for his Reconstruction policies and preferred congressional candidates, Johnson embarked on an unsuccessful national tour. (Whipple argued that he did so “with the intention of carrying the country by assault.”) His endeavors wound up hurting, rather than helping, his cause. He took to the stump to advocate for his own interests, with Whipple noting “the immense protuberance” of the first-person pronoun throughout the president’s many speeches. Although he didn’t make the posteriors of his political allies central to his closing argument, in the end, he was deemed a “Presidential Ass” by a Michigan Republican. Such presidential barnstorming amid a congressional election was something of a novelty that many deemed beneath the dignity of the office; the intemperate content of Johnson’s speeches made it worse. His remarks at times devolved into “a volcanic outbreak of vulgarity, conceit, bombast, scurrility, ignorance, insolence, brutality, and balderdash,” according to Whipple. When Johnson found himself assailed by hecklers (who he claimed were paid disrupters), his material took dark and strange turns. After one audience member called for the hanging of the Confederate president, Jefferson Davis, Johnson in turn suggested hanging the Republican representative Thaddeus Stevens and the abolitionist Wendell Phillips. Subsequent jeers inspired him to compare himself to Christ, betrayed by Judas and suffering on behalf of the nation at large. Governors, mayors, and other politicians were reportedly avoiding the president’s appearances, sometimes declining to welcome him or leaving town before he arrived. As the tour concluded in the middle of September, the magnitude of Johnson’s mistake came into view. By one senator’s estimate, Johnson’s campaigning cost his preferred candidates roughly a million votes across the country—no small number in that era’s electorate. The New York Times reportedly lost nearly a third of its mostly Republican subscribers after its editor, Henry Jarvis Raymond, had openly supported Johnson and the National Union movement. Most important, the very Republicans whom Johnson had wished to displace didn’t lose seats but gained them, beyond the two-thirds majority necessary to override the presidential veto that Johnson had already used against Reconstruction legislation. And Johnson, for his part, later became the first president to ever be impeached. The 1866 midterms took place in an entirely different world from ours. A president campaigning on behalf of congressional candidates was uncommon then, and a president routinely violating the decorum and propriety associated with the office was more uncommon yet. Whipple hoped that voters would go on to “indignantly record the most overwhelming of verdicts” against Johnson. Now, 160 years later, America once more has a president who has elevated his own ambitions above the nation’s. The people’s verdict awaits.

items.title: GES cautions teachers against paying money for automatic promotion
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has cautioned teachers participating in its ongoing promotion examination against paying money to individuals who claim they can secure them automatic promotion. The warning follows reports received by management that some unscrupulous individuals are demanding money from candidates under the pretext of facilitating their promotion. In a press release issued on Tuesday, November 3, the Service stressed that the promotion exercise was transparent and strictly merit-based, insisting that no payment or financial inducement was required or could guarantee a candidate’s promotion. Management, therefore, urged all eligible staff participating in the examination to disregard such demands and refrain from making payments to anyone in exchange for promises of promotion. The Service also encouraged candidates to approach the examination with confidence, dedication and a positive attitude, while wishing them success in the exercise. It further called on staff who encounter individuals soliciting money or have information about such fraudulent activities to report the matter to the police. The GES reiterated that promotion would be determined solely by merit and the established procedures, warning candidates against falling victim to individuals seeking to exploit the exercise for financial gain.

items.title: ‘Yɛgye Yɛ Sika’ demo: NPP on ‘fishing expedition’ against Ablakwa – NDC
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) of targeting Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa because of his record in exposing alleged corruption. The party described the NPP’s demands for accountability over the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa as a “fishing expedition”, arguing that the party is attempting to discredit the minister through repeated allegations. Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story on Tuesday, November 3, following the NPP’s ‘Yɛgye Yɛ Sika’ demonstration, the National Deputy Communications Director of the NDC, Julius Kwame Anthony, said the opposition was determined to make an example of Mr Ablakwa to discourage others from challenging corruption. “In fact, I have earlier described them as a group of people who are deep-necked into corruption and see all who have fought corruption in one way or the other as enemies to their cause. “And they are very desperate to ensure that they make an example of such people so that nobody else will set such an example, the conduct of those people in the fight against corruption under their administration ever again. The Honourable Okudzeto Ablakwa is just being targeted by the NPP. They are on a fishing expedition,” he said. The NPP staged the demonstration to demand accountability over the evacuation arrangements and called for the removal of Mr Ablakwa. Read also: ‘Yɛgye Yɛ Sika’: NPP youth wing protests over SA evacuation expenditure, diplomatic passports Mr Anthony accused the opposition of repeatedly making allegations against the minister in the hope that some would eventually gain public acceptance. “They are on a fishing expedition. They are on a consistent mass slinging, throwing one, if it fails to throw another, with the hope that with time some of it would stick and that other people will watch it and fear that in the events that the people of this country are bedeviled with an NPP administration, they would fear going against that attitude of corruption, which characterized the previous NPP administration,” he said. He maintained that Mr Ablakwa, during his time in opposition, relied on what he described as credible evidence when raising concerns about alleged wrongdoing under the previous NPP administration. He contrasted this with the NPP’s current demand for invoices relating to chartered flights used in the evacuation exercise, questioning why a political party should receive such documents directly from a state institution. “I ask myself, at what point in the history of the Republic of Ghana do we have a situation where invoices of transactions of state institutions are sent to the headquarters of political parties? In this case, the NPP is demanding that we bring invoices of chartered flights to them at Asylum Down. At what point does accountability mean that?” he questioned. He said that concerns about possible financial irregularities in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs should be investigated through the appropriate state institutions. “If you want accountability and you want to check whether or not there are any infractions in the dealings of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, an audit properly conducted by the institutions of state designated to do so would bring those answers,” he said.

items.title: FG policies raise Nigeria’s exports by 25% – Dantsoho
items.description: Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), says Federal Government policies and reforms have increased Nigeria’s exports by 25 per cent in the last two years. Dantsoho said this on Tuesday at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH) in London. Mr Ikechukwu Onyemekara, NPA’s General Manager, Corporate Communication and Strategy, disclosed this in a statement made available to newsmen in Lagos. Dantsoho said that Nigeria’s large population offered the country significant economic advantages, while recent reforms had contributed to increased cargo throughput and export volumes. He said that the growth covered not only oil and gas but also manufactured goods, agricultural products, including cocoa and cashew, as well as raw materials. He attributed the development to improved collaboration between the NPA and major terminal operators, including APM Terminals, which had enhanced operational efficiency, export volumes and port competitiveness. The NPA boss said that the authority had established about four Export Processing Terminals to streamline export operations. He explained that the terminals operated in collaboration with terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies to ensure that export cargo was processed locally before shipment. According to him, the arrangement ensures that Nigerian export products meet international standards and reduces challenges associated with quality compliance in destination markets. Dantsoho said that Nigeria was better positioned to benefit from the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) through the reforms introduced by the administration of President Bola Tinubu. He said that the reforms had strengthened the economy and attracted investors, creating opportunities for increased trade and cooperation among African countries. He cited Nigeria’s growing trade relations with Morocco, particularly in the manufacturing sector, noting that the North African country had emerged as a hub for electric vehicle and smaller vehicle production. Dantsoho also attributed Nigeria’s improved global port ranking to the reforms, noting that two Nigerian ports featured among the top 20 in the latest World Bank global ports ranking. He described the achievement as a result of improved efficiency, technology adoption and effective collaboration with industry stakeholders. The NPA managing director further disclosed that revenue generated from ports across the country had quadrupled, driven by increased cargo volumes and partnerships with international investors and terminal operators. He said that Nigerian ports had recorded significant improvements in efficiency compared with other ports in West Africa. Dantsoho, who is also President of the Association of Ports in West and Central Africa, acknowledged improvements in port operations in countries such as Tanzania and Kenya. He, however, stressed the need for African countries to strengthen collaboration and sustain ongoing reforms to enhance the continent’s competitiveness. He said that government was investing one billion dollars in the expansion and modernisation of Apapa Port in Lagos to accommodate future growth and improve competitiveness. “Expansion and modernisation require collaboration with the private sector. “NPA is working with APM Terminals and other major players with the required capital, alongside technology partners from Singapore and elsewhere,” he said. Dantsoho also said the NPA developed a Single Window system in 2025 in partnership with a Singaporean firm. He added that the authority was collaborating with a company in Abu Dhabi to develop a Port Community System aimed at strengthening business-to-business relationships and improving port operations. (NAN) The post FG policies raise Nigeria’s exports by 25% – Dantsoho appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NPP questions Ablakwa’s figures in South Africa evacuation, demands independent audit
items.description: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has questioned the figures provided by Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa, insisting that an independent audit is needed to establish the actual cost and number of people transported. He rejected the minister’s decision to invite the Auditor-General to conduct a special audit of evacuation exercises dating back to 2017, arguing that the process should instead be handled by an independent audit firm whose findings would be made public. Speaking on JoyFM’ s Top Story on Tuesday, November 3, the National Youth Organiser of the NPP, Abanga Fuseini Yakubu, said the party did not have confidence in an audit process initiated by the minister, who is at the centre of the controversy. “What Okudzeto Ablakwa is doing, it is like you having an issue with me and inviting me into your court where you are the same judge in that court and you are going to determine the case. It doesn’t make sense, and we don’t believe in certain investigations,” he said. The NPP youth organiser said his party wanted an independent audit of the entire evacuation exercise, with the findings published to the public. He also raised questions about figures contained in a document released by the Foreign Affairs Ministry following a Right to Information request by the NPP Minority in Parliament. According to him, the document indicated that 1,964 people were evacuated from South Africa to Ghana, while three chartered flights, each with a capacity of about 300 passengers, were used. He questioned how the remaining passengers were transported and demanded details of the commercial flights allegedly used, including ticket costs, passenger manifests, seat numbers, and payment vouchers. “The charter flight carries 300 people, which he chartered three flights. So 300 times three adds up to 900. So leaving the rest of the people on the plane. And that is how we want to know whether those people came with a commercial flight, whether they came with cars or bicycles, how much did he pay for each ticket, each flight, and which seat numbers, the vouchers, the passenger manifest. “These are legitimate concerns that we are asking for. And we are also asking for the publication of the receipt that he paid for the $750,000 for the charter flight. Because in the commercial market, those ordinarily would not cost more than $150,000 to $300,000.” On concerns raised about commercial flight records, including the identification of only 247 passengers against the minister’s reported figure of more than 1,000, Mr Yakubu said the NPP was seeking documentary evidence to establish the actual number of passengers transported. Read also: ‘Yɛgye Yɛ Sika’: NPP youth wing protests over SA evacuation expenditure, diplomatic passports He maintained that the party’s concerns were not politically motivated, citing JoyNews’ investigations into the evacuation arrangements as evidence that the questions raised deserved attention. “I can refer Joy News. The guys who did that wonderful job, I don’t believe they are politicians. They only say what they see. And the New Patriotic Party Minority in Parliament are on the same page with what Joy FM did,” he said. He questioned why the minister and members of the NDC would dismiss the NPP’s concerns on political grounds when, in his view, the media investigation had also raised questions about the exercise.

items.title: MoFA, DMT sign MoU for 21,000-tonne grain storage facility in Wa
items.description: The Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with DMT Collateral Management Limited for the construction of a 21,000-tonne grain storage facility in Wa in the Upper West Region. The agreement, signed on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at the Ministry in Accra, forms part of efforts under the government’s Feed Ghana Programme to expand the country’s grain storage capacity, minimise post-harvest losses and strengthen national food security. The facility is expected to serve as a Food Security Hub, providing strategic grain reserves to support the country during periods of food shortages and other emergencies. Speaking at the signing ceremony, the Minister for Food and Agriculture, Eric Opoku, commended DMT Collateral Management Limited and the Danish Embassy for their role in facilitating the project. He reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to supporting the successful implementation of the facility. The Chief Executive Officer of DMT Collateral Management Limited, Paul Sannie Minlah, said the project would incorporate an emergency grain reserve system known as the Hospital Bin , designed to ensure the availability of food stocks during periods of national need. The project will be supported by an export credit of approximately €4.8 million facilitated by the Danish Embassy, alongside an additional investment of about €5 million. Beyond improving grain storage, the facility is also expected to create training opportunities for National Service personnel, members of the Feed Ghana Brigades and Ghanaian technicians. The training will focus on silo operations, grain handling and maintenance to build local technical capacity and support the efficient management of the facility. The project is expected to be completed and commissioned by August 2027.

items.title: AES : le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger préparent des accords pour accélérer leur intégration numérique
items.description: Le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger entendent donner une traduction concrète à leur coopération dans les domaines du numérique, des postes et des communications électroniques. Réunis du 3 au 5 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, les experts des trois pays travaillent à la finalisation des documents techniques nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des activités inscrites dans la Feuille de route de l’An II de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES). La cérémonie d’ouverture, coprésidée par les ministres chargés du numérique des trois pays, a été marquée par une volonté commune : faire aboutir les chantiers engagés et passer des orientations stratégiques à des réalisations concrètes. Pour le ministre burkinabè de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, Dr Aminata ZERBO/SABANÉ, cette rencontre doit permettre de franchir un cap dans l'opérationnalisation des engagements communautaires. Elle a salué la mobilisation des délégations sœurs du Mali et du Niger, tout en rappelant le rôle du numérique comme levier d’intégration et de développement de l’espace sahélien. Cinq chantiers majeurs structurent les travaux : l’interconnexion et le partage des infrastructures numériques, le développement d’un hub régional pour les opérateurs satellitaires NGSO, l’achat groupé de capacité de bande passante Internet, la mise en place d’un dispositif régional de réponse aux incidents informatiques, ainsi que la modernisation et l’intégration des services postaux. Au terme des trois jours, les experts devront produire des documents directement exploitables : protocoles d’accord, notes conceptuelles, schémas d’architecture et calendriers d’exécution. Ces livrables serviront de base aux conventions dont la signature est prévue en marge de la Semaine du Numérique, du 24 au 27 novembre 2026 au Burkina Faso. « La tâche qui vous est confiée est exigeante », a rappelé la ministre burkinabè aux participants, les exhortant à faire preuve de rigueur, de créativité et d’esprit de fraternité pour parvenir à des propositions consensuelles et réalistes. À travers cette démarche, les trois pays veulent construire des réponses communes à des préoccupations partagées : améliorer la connectivité, réduire les coûts d’accès à Internet, mieux protéger les infrastructures numériques et rapprocher les services postaux des populations. L'enjeu est désormais de traduire cette volonté politique commune en accords opérationnels et en actions mesurables, au bénéfice des populations de la Confédération des États du Sahel. Source : DCRP/MTDPCE

items.title: Ballot machine glitch hits New York county in tight House race
items.description: Ballot machines malfunctioned in a hotly contested House race in New York state Tuesday, prompting right-wing influencers to fling unfounded allegations of US midterms voter fraud even as local election officials insisted all ballots would be counted. President Donald Trump and his allies have previously spread unproven claims about voting machines, alleging that they are faulty or unreliable. The Westchester County Board of Elections said it was aware of an issue involving paper ballots that is preventing voting machines from accepting ballots at polling locations throughout the county. The board “wants to reassure every voter that your vote matters, your ballot will be secure and your vote will be counted,” with ballots instead placed in emergency bags, it said in a statement. Parts of Westchester County are included in New York’s 17th district, where incumbent Republican Mike Lawler faces Democrat Cait Conley in a House of Representatives seat that voted for Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. Pro-Donald Trump influencers pounced on the glitch by claiming, without evidence, that Democrats were trying to “steal” the election. They included conspiracy theorist Laura Loomer, conservative activist Scott Pressler, and Katie Miller, a podcaster married to White House advisor Stephen Miller. The New York State Board of Elections said on X that there has been no disruption to voting. “Long-established emergency ballot procedures have been implemented, where completed ballots are secured, under bipartisan control, and will be counted,” it said. The Board added in a later statement that the technical error was linked to voting machines being unable to read and accept the ballots. “Importantly, the affected scanners rejected ballots they could not properly recognize rather than incorrectly tabulating them,” it said. The post Ballot machine glitch hits New York county in tight House race appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Última hora del accidente de trenes de Urda, en Toledo, en directo | Óscar Puente dimite: “Un ministro no puede continuar en su puesto con un accidente de este tipo”
items.description: El ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, ha anunciado su dimisión tras la tragedia ferroviaria que ha causado 69 víctimas mortales en Urda: “Un ministro de Transportes de un país como España no puede continuar en su cargo tras dos accidentes en menos de un año”, ha lanzado el ministro al final de una comparecencia de cuatro horas en el Congreso para dar cuenta del accidente. El ministro ha comunicado su decisión al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, apenas minutos antes de hacerla pública, y el presidente ha elogiado luego su gesto: “Ha dado la cara, soluciones y, después, un paso al lado”. Durante un tenso y bronco debate, Puente ha recordado que su Gobierno puso en marcha un plan de renovación de 780 millones de euros y ha reiterado las dudas sobre la decisión del centro de control de Adif de autorizar al AVE implicado en el accidente de Urda (Toledo) a reanudar la circulación en marcha normal, pese a la caída del sistema de seguridad LZB y a que había un tren de Iryo detenido más adelante. Tras el anuncio del ministro, el PP ha achacado su decisión a un cálculo político: “No se va por las víctimas ni por dignidad, sino por la encuestas”, han señalado fuentes de Génova. Minutos antes, durante el debate, la portavoz del PP, Ester Muñoz, había replicado al ministro que su responsabilidad “no es explicar accidentes mortales”, sino evitarlos. Sumar también había pedido su dimisión, aunque aclaraba que no le atribuía la culpa del accidente. Por su parte, el portavoz de ERC, Gabriel Rufián, había insistido en que un error humano refleja “un sistema de seguridad fallido”. El accidente ha dejado 69 muertos y alrededor de 200 heridos, 40 de ellos aún hospitalizados. Seguir leyendo

items.title: APC rejects Tinubu campaign council list in Osun, demands review
items.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun has rejected its State Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) list, alleging breaches of party guidelines and exclusion of key officials. Mr Wole Adunola, Osun APC Publicity Secretary, disclosed this in a statement jointly signed by two other party officials on Tuesday in Abuja. Adunola said the list failed to reflect due process, inclusiveness and respect for established party structures. He said the exclusion of several State Working Committee members, who should be statutory members, informed the rejection. “Of particular concern is the omission of several members of the State Working Committee who, according to applicable guidelines, are expected to be statutory members of the council,” he said. Adunola said the exclusion raised concerns about consultation, due process and respect for the party’s established leadership structure. He also questioned the composition of the council in relation to an earlier presidential directive reportedly naming Gov. Ademola Adeleke as its Director-General. According to him, Adeleke subsequently inaugurated a broad-based campaign team to coordinate President Bola Tinubu’s presidential campaign across the state. Adunola said it was unclear why a different structure had emerged without adequate clarification or alignment with the existing arrangement. He suggested that the newly released list might have been intended for a Parliamentary Campaign Council rather than the PCC. “If the newly released list was intended to serve as a Parliamentary Campaign Council rather than the PCC, its composition would be more understandable,” he said. Adunola said the distinction must be clarified to prevent confusion, duplication of responsibilities and unnecessary friction within the party’s campaign structure. He stressed that the State Executive Committee remained integral to the APC’s organisational framework and should not be sidelined. “A successful campaign must be built on mutual respect, proper coordination, and the active involvement of legitimate party stakeholders,” he said. Adunola called for an immediate review of the list, with consultations involving relevant stakeholders, including APC National Secretary, Sen. Surajudeen Basiru, and the State Director-General. He said the consultations would ensure proper alignment, effective coordination and respect for established party procedures. Adunola reaffirmed the chapter’s commitment to Tinubu’s re-election bid and the overall interests of the APC. He, however, warned that party loyalty should not prevent constructive engagement when decisions risk creating avoidable divisions and undermining collective efforts. He urged party leaders at state and national levels to address the concerns promptly and make the necessary corrections. Adunola said an effective campaign council must accommodate legitimate stakeholders, recognise established leadership and unite members towards electoral victory. items.title: Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats
items.description: Seven passenger planes across Europe, two of which departed from the UK, have been inspected following a series of suspected bomb threats. Two Ryanair flights, one originating from Dublin and the other from Lisbon, were searched after landing in Rome following anonymous tips but no explosives were found, sources at the city’s Fiumicino airport told the BBC. The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air Force until landing. Authorities have also searched planes in Poland, Spain and Bulgaria. While officially there is no link between them, authorities from various countries will be co-operating to assess whether this was a co-ordinated attack, designed to disrupt airspace. The UK government described today’s incidents as “malicious hoax threats”. In a statement it said it had “one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we’ve seen today”. Aviation security expert Paul Mason said bomb threats on passenger planes “don’t happen that frequently”, which made the latest incidents “unusual”. “It sounds like they’ve been made in a credible manner across a broad range of airlines,” Mason told BBC Radio 5 Live. “That would suggest to me that it’s been a very deliberate act by a typical actor rather than a load of coincidental, malicious calls.” He said “there are a lot of processes” that the onboard crew and people on the ground must go through “to validate the credibility of the threat”. A flight may be asked to divert if the credibility of a threat “is of a certain level”, Mason added, and in some cases the onboard crew may not even be advised on what the ground operators were dealing with. Two of the four flights were en route to Warsaw Chopin airport In Rome, sources at Fiumicino airport told the BBC police bomb disposal experts carried out standard security protocols to ensure the safety of all passengers and crew. Inspections of the passengers, luggage, and the aircraft yielded negative results, and the alert has since been cleared. One plane which landed in Murcia, southern Spain – a Ryanair flight coming from Manchester – was also found not to have any explosives on board, Spanish authorities said. One passenger later said she was unaware of the bomb threat until after the plane landed. “We weren’t told anything during the flight,” Sarah told BBC Radio 5 Live. “The plane stopped quite suddenly and then we were kept on the runway for around 30 minutes.” “Then the fire engines turned up, the bomb squad turned up and we were asked to evacuate,” she continues. Sarah said the plane had not been on the ground a minute before it was “surrounded by fire engines and police and a bomb squad”. All the passengers were then escorted by police, leaving all their belongings. “We were only later told that it was an actual threat, a bomb threat to the plane itself,” she added. Two flights heading to Warsaw were also affected, including one from London Heathrow. The Heathrow flight was originally meant to land at the Polish capital’s main airport, Chopin, but was diverted instead to the smaller Modlin airport, briefly forcing its closure. A Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen to Warsaw-Chopin landed as planned. Later on Tuesday, Bulgarian Transport Minister Georgi Peev said there were bomb threats against two planes travelling to the country’s capital Sofia. He told the state-owned Bulgarian News Agency (BTA) the flights were from the northern Italian city of Bergamo and Ireland’s capital Dublin. The flights into Sofia were not diverted and no explosives were found when the planes were checked, Peev said. Bulgaria’s border police said in a statement sent to the BBC that at around 10:35 (08:35 GMT) it had received an email about “the presence of an improvised explosive device on a flight returning from Bergamo”. “Standard procedures for such incidents were immediately activated, and an operational headquarters comprising representatives of various institutions was convened,” the statement said. The border police added that the same email also reported a “similar threat against aircraft arriving from Dublin”. Initial checks found no explosives on board the Crown Iris cruise ship In a separate development, a bomb alert triggered the evacuation of 1,537 passengers and crew from an Israel-bound cruise ship in Greece, media reports from both countries say. Initial checks of the Panama-flagged Crown Iris vessel currently docked at a port on the Aegean island of Syros found no explosives, they said citing the Greek Coast Guard. A second inspection is expected shortly. Tuesday’s aircraft incidents come a day after a Wizz Air flight from London Luton made an emergency landing in Budapest, escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet, after a bomb threat. Wizz Air said later that security checks had been made and nothing was found. BBC Verify has consulted aviation safety experts about what happens on board a plane when a bomb threat is issued. Marco Chan, a former pilot for Cathay Pacific Airways and Hong Kong Airlines who is now a senior lecturer in aviation operations at Kingston University, said a bomb threat is considered “genuine until it is resolved, even though most turn out to be hoaxes”. Chan said crews will “quietly search” toilets, galleys and storage areas and will not touch a suspicious item unless it has to be taken to an area on the aircraft designated as the least risky bomb location. The aircraft’s captain will have multiple factors to assess, according to former airline pilot Terry Tozer, an aviation safety commentator. He said these include what facilities are available at the airport they are being diverted to and how the plane can continue onwards should it turn out to be a false threat. Chan added that once on the ground, the plane is generally “taken to an isolated stand, passengers are disembarked, and police and bomb disposal teams search it”.

items.title: Six Books You Should Read Twice
items.description: In the seven years I taught writing to first-year university students, I always began the semester the same way: We’d start with lessons on how to read critically. To help them, I introduced the concept of the hermeneutic circle—a fancy philosophical name for a simple idea. To comprehend the meaning of a book, readers need to analyze its individual sentences and paragraphs, but those parts can’t be interpreted without understanding how they work as a whole. In practice, this usually means reading to the end and going right back to the beginning. The hermeneutic circle isn’t just for academics, though; it explains why some novels feel impossible to put down. You’re using it when you flip back to the opening of a mystery after you’ve reached a pivotal scene that changes what you thought you knew. Sometimes a plot twist completely flips your understanding of a character, and you can’t help but reread the novel, this time with your eyes wide open. The six books below feature unreliable narrators, jarring perspective shifts, and slow-burning reveals. As soon as they’re over, they demand to be instantly started again. Devil House , by John Darnielle Darnielle, the front man for the indie band the Mountain Goats, starts his third novel simply enough. Gage Chandler, a once-acclaimed true-crime writer, is sniffing out what just might be his next hit: an investigation into a 1986 unsolved double murder at a former porn shop. Some 20 years later, Chandler has moved into the scene of the crime, dubbed “Devil House,” to immerse himself in the story. But the more time he spends going through grisly source material purchased from eBay, the more he chafes at his task. Then Darnielle takes Devil House down a series of sharp left turns, and each new section feels like its own book: This meta-novel grows to include the story of the crime that inspired Chandler’s debut, The White Witch of Morro Bay , and a faux–Middle English myth rendered in Gothic font. Darnielle’s eventual return to Devil House—and Chandler’s accounting of the costs of digging up its history—is no less surprising. The reader is left to reassemble this dissection of the true-crime genre, and then to ponder what it means to arrange jumbled puzzle pieces into a coherent portrait. [ Read: 15 books you won’t regret rereading ] Dirtbag, Massachusetts , by Isaac Fitzgerald Though his memoir-in-essays is subtitled A Confessional , and though it opens by revising the story he and his family used to tell about his childhood, Fitzgerald doesn’t immediately lay bare the lingering pain of his tumultuous upbringing. The first 11 essays are plenty vulnerable: Fitzgerald writes that he was born of an affair; spent his early years living in a homeless shelter and then in low-income housing run by the Catholic Worker movement; moved to north-central Massachusetts, where “violence was the solution, problem, and consequence”; and began abusing alcohol and drugs before age 13. But these are mere “flashes of the past,” as Fitzgerald writes in the last essay, “My Story,” where he takes full control of the narrative of his life. As he admits to having avoided the full truth, Fitzgerald becomes his own confessor, the one with the power to forgive. Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead , by Olga Tokarczuk, trans lated by Antonia Lloyd-Jones Janina Duszejko, the strange older woman who narrates this Nobel Laureate’s fairy tale–tinged noir thriller, seems too caught up in her devotion to animals, astrology, and the poetry of William Blake to involve herself in anything as petty as a whodunit. But when poachers start turning up dead in Duszejko’s remote Polish hamlet in the Kłodzko Valley, she fights to make the police listen to her theory of the crimes: The animals who have long made their home in the village’s bordering forest are taking their revenge. In Tokarczuk’s hands, Duszejko is no “crazy madwoman,” as the police see her, but a prophet—the only one who can see that “animals have a very strong sense of justice.” On a second pass, with full knowledge of why Duszejko becomes so wrapped up in the murder investigations, you can better appreciate how Tokarczuk subverts the thriller’s typical form with a philosophical meditation on how humans have become all too comfortable with destroying the natural world. [ Read: The case for rereading the high-school classics ] Loved and Missed , by Susie Boyt I picked up Loved and Missed after seeing it recommended again and again by fellow critics as a touching, engrossing novel about the pleasures of caregiving , one that they were desperate to talk about. The book—largely narrated by a middle-aged schoolteacher named Ruth as she takes over the parenting of her granddaughter, Lily, from her drug-addicted daughter, Eleanor—is indeed poignant and charming. Ruth builds a cozy home life after deciding that Lily “was not going to have a poultice childhood, a mending service, scrappy and provisional.” Yet buzzing beneath this domestic bliss is the live wire of Eleanor’s presence and absence, and the reader is forced to wonder how Lily is affected by being the object of all of Ruth’s displaced motherly love. Then, in the last chapter, Boyt hands the reins of narration to the teenage Lily, adding a fresh charge to all that came before. No wonder we can’t stop talking about it. She’s Under Here: A Love Story, a Horror Story, a Reckoning , by Karen Palmer The first time I read Palmer’s memoir of fleeing her abusive ex-husband and assuming a new identity, I hardly came up for air. I was fully submerged in her recounting of 14 dangerous years of marriage—including a harrowing scene of her ex holding a gun to her pregnant belly—followed by escalating torment after she flees with her daughters. But this memoir of surviving domestic violence and then coming to terms with what it costs to start over entirely, including forged birth certificates and a fake life story, deserves to be lingered over, just as Palmer’s fear stayed with her for decades. Only on my second read, once I had made it through with Palmer to safer shores, was I able to fully appreciate the author’s persistent doubts about the choices she was forced to make, as well her haunting meditations on why she stayed for so long. [ Read: What rereading childhood books teaches adults about themselves ] Women and Children First , by Alina Grabowski The fictional decaying coastal town of Nashquitten, Massachusetts, is a place where “it seemed like there was a death every month”—opioid overdoses, drunk driving, suicides. But the mysterious death of the aspiring artist Lucy Anderson at a high-school party stands out. Grabowski follows the ripples and rifts that led to and came after Lucy’s demise via a Rashomon -like structure, switching among the perspectives of 10 different girls and women connected to Lucy: her classmate, her guidance counselor, her best friend, her mother. Each narrator’s story offers a shard of what happened at that party, yet their points of view are contradictory and hopelessly biased, each coloring the reader’s understanding of what came before. Women and Children First is less a puzzle than a kaleidoscope, offering several misaligned but interconnected visions of the truth. The satisfaction comes not from any definitive reveal of what happened to Lucy, but from unraveling how all these characters’ actions and stories affect one another—something you can only really understand once you’ve finished the book and gone back to page one.

items.title: Élections régionales et sénatoriales : le président Doumbouya convoque le corps électoral (décret)
items.description: Dans un décret diffusé dans la soirée de ce mardi 3 novembre 2026 à la télévision nationale, le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, a procédé à la convocation du corps électoral pour les élections régionales du 29 novembre 2026 et les élections sénatoriales du 20 décembre 2026. « Article 1er : Le corps électoral est convoqué le dimanche 29 novembre 2026 sur l'ensemble du territoire national en vue de procéder à l'élection des conseillers régionaux. Le collège électoral appelé à prendre part à ce scrutin est constitué des conseillers communaux conformément aux dispositions légales du code électoral. ​ Article 2 : Le corps électoral est également convoqué le dimanche 20 décembre 2026 en vue de procéder à l'élection des deux tiers des sénateurs conformément aux dispositions du code électoral. Le collège électoral appelé à prendre part à ce scrutin est constitué des conseillers régionaux et des conseillers communaux. ​ Article 3 : Le nombre d'électeurs inscrits pour les élections régionales du 29 novembre 2026 est fixé à 7 873. Le nombre d'électeurs inscrits pour l'élection sénatoriale du 20 décembre 2026 est fixé à 8 780. ​ Article 4 : La ministre de l'Administration du Territoire et de la Décentralisation, le ministre de la Justice et des Droits de l'Homme, le ministre de la Sécurité et de la Protection civile, le ministre délégué auprès du Président de la République chargé de la Défense nationale, le ministre de l'Économie, des Finances et du Budget, ainsi que les responsables des institutions et services compétents en la matière électorale sont chargés, chacun en ce qui le concerne, de l'application du présent décret. ​ Article 5 : Le présent décret, qui abroge toutes dispositions antérieures contraires, prend effet à compter de la date de sa signature et sera enregistré et publié au Journal officiel de la République », précise le décret.
