items.title: Hausse des prix des carburants : le gouvernement aura-t-il les mains libres en 2027 ?
items.description: Le gouvernement aura-t-il les mains libres pour revoir à la hausse les prix des carburants sans passer par le Parlement en 2027 ? L’article 218 du projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027 propose à ce que les prix des carburants puissent « faire l’objet de révision, en cas de besoin, par les parties prenantes », sans préciser ces dernières. Une disposition qui ouvre la voie à d’éventuelles hausses des prix de l’essence, du gasoil et du GPLc. Mais cette proposition risque de ne pas passer. La commission des finances et du budget de l'Assemblée populaire nationale (APN) a proposé 26 amendements de fond au PLF 2026 dont un concerne les carburants. La Commission veut soumettre « toute révision des prix des carburants » par les parties prenantes à « l'approbation » du Parlement, dans le cadre de la loi de finances. Cet amendement a un double objectif, selon la commission : la « transparence » et la « protection du pouvoir d'achat des citoyens. » Hausse des prix des carburants : la Commission des Finances de l’APN s’oppose au gouvernement La commission a justifié son désaccord avec le gouvernement sur la question des carburants par « la nécessité de consacrer le caractère social de l'Etat et de garantir la conformité avec les constantes nationales de l'Algérie, en associant les représentants du peuple à toute augmentation ou révision des prix des carburants », a expliqué le rapporteur, selon l’agence APS. Dans l’exposé des motifs de la proposition de ne pas soumettre la hausse des prix des carburants au vote du Parlement, le gouvernement a rappelé que l’État maintient une politique de tarification de l’essence, du gasoil et du GPLc “parmi les plus avantageuses et stables au monde, visant à soutenir durablement le modèle énergétique national”. L’article Hausse des prix des carburants : le gouvernement aura-t-il les mains libres en 2027 ? est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Olodo murder: Police arrest two suspects, deploy Army, Amotekun
items.description: .as tension grips Ibadan community By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Police Command has arrested two suspects in connection with the killing of a 26-year-old man, identified as Kehinde Asimiyu, following a fatal altercation at Olodo Garage in the Lagelu Local Government Area of Ibadan, while reinforcing security in the area to prevent a breakdown of law and order. The development came amid heightened tension in the Olodo community following the fatal stabbing of the young man, popularly known as KBlaq, by a commercial motorcyclist during a disagreement over transport fare, an incident that disrupted commercial activities and forced residents and commuters to trek considerable distances after motorcycle operators withdrew their services over fears of possible reprisal attacks. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, said the command received a report of the incident on 1 November 2026, indicating that the deceased had allegedly been stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde following an altercation between the two men at Olodo Garage. According to the police, “the deceased was allegedly stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde at Olodo Garage following an altercation between both parties.” The statement added that the incident subsequently came to the attention of the deceased’s family when “an unidentified motorcycle rider arrived at their residence and informed them of the attack.” “Following receipt of the report, police operatives, accompanied by a patrol team, immediately mobilised to the scene, while the victim was rushed to Academy Hospital, Texaco, Iwo Road, Ibadan, where he was confirmed dead by the doctor on duty.“ “His remains were subsequently deposited at Adejare Embalming Centre for preservation, while photographs were taken as part of the preliminary investigative procedures.“ The police said investigations into the circumstances surrounding the killing had led to the arrest of two suspects, identified as Taiwo Babarinde, suspected to have inflicted the fatal injury on the deceased, and Ishola Semiu, suspected of involvement in the incident. “Both suspects are currently in Police custody, while the case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Iyaganku, Ibadan, for comprehensive investigation,” the statement said. However, the police intervention following the killing also witnessed a fresh security challenge, as unrest reportedly erupted at the Olodo Police Outpost, nearly resulting in a breakdown of law and order. The situation was further compounded by subsequent reports of threats from hoodlums, prompting the immediate reinforcement of security across the area to prevent further disturbances and protect residents. Consequently, the Commissioner of Police, CP Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, directed the deployment of additional operational assets, with personnel of the Nigerian Army, Amotekun Corps, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and other local law enforcement components joining the security operation. The command said the coordinated deployment had helped restore normalcy, adding that there was now a sustained security presence in the area “to forestall further disturbances and protect residents.” In a further move to address the underlying tensions, the Commissioner of Police directed the Area Commander, Moniya, to engage relevant community stakeholders towards addressing the situation and preventing a recurrence. Acting on the directive, the Area Commander earlier on Tuesday held a strategic meeting with representatives of the Local Council Development Area (LCDA), leaders of tricycle and motorcycle operators, as well as youth leaders. The engagement, according to the police, “focused on identifying practical solutions, strengthening communication with security agencies and promoting peaceful coexistence among residents and other stakeholders.” Reassuring residents of the command’s commitment to their safety, the police said: “The Command reassures residents of Olodo and its environs that adequate security measures remain in place to safeguard lives and property.” The command also issued a stern warning to those seeking to exploit the situation to foment trouble, incite violence or destabilise the area. “It also issues a stern warning to individuals or groups seeking to foment trouble, incite violence or exploit the situation to destabilise the area that such conduct will not be tolerated,” the statement added. It further declared that: “The Command will decisively deal with anyone whose actions threaten public peace or undermine the security gains recorded across Oyo State.” The Commissioner of Police also appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid actions capable of escalating the crisis. He urged them to “remain calm, shun violence and embrace dialogue as a means of resolving disagreements.” He further encouraged community members to cooperate with security agencies by providing credible and timely information, while reiterating the command’s determination to sustain the prevailing peace and ensure the safety and security of all residents. The post Olodo murder: Police arrest two suspects, deploy Army, Amotekun appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: En attendant… véto !
items.description: Il aura fallu cinquante ans de diplomatie, trente-cinq ans de présence onusienne, une interminable procession de résolutions et, pour finir, un veto russe pour que la question du Sahara connaisse l'un de ces retournements dont l'Histoire a le secret – et dont elle semble, cette fois, s'être particulièrement amusée. L'affaire du Sahara ! Ce caillou dans les babouches du Maroc, cette pierre de Sisyphe que le Royaume pousse depuis un demi-siècle, ce dossier dont certains avaient fini par faire une profession, d'autres une rente et quelques-uns une véritable raison d'être politique. Le paradoxe est saisissant. C'est le Maroc lui-même qui avait porté devant les Nations unies la question du Sahara, alors sous administration espagnole, pour mettre fin à une présence coloniale sur une terre qui n'avait jamais cessé d'être la sienne. C'est encore lui qui aspire aujourd'hui à refermer un chapitre onusien devenu interminable. Entre ces deux moments : une Marche verte, une guerre, un cessez-le-feu, des négociations, des impasses, des retournements d'alliances et parfois, reconnaissons-le, quelques erreurs de casting diplomatique bien de chez nous, particulièrement durant les décennies 1970 à 1990. Il y eut aussi ce voisinage compliqué, marqué par l'héritage de Houari Boumédiène, dont la politique saharienne a durablement structuré la rivalité algéro-marocaine. Et puis vint octobre 2026. Le veto russe : venu casser, reparti en bâtisseur Le 30 octobre, le Conseil de sécurité examine deux projets concurrents. Le premier, américain, entend réorganiser la mission onusienne et placer plus explicitement le plan marocain d'autonomie au centre du processus politique. Il recueille onze voix favorables, mais se heurte au veto russe. Le second, présenté par Moscou, vise essentiellement à prolonger la MINURSO sans toucher à son mandat. Il échoue à son tour. Résultat : personne n'obtient sa résolution et la mission, créée en 1991, se retrouve sans mandat renouvelé. Le 1er novembre, le secrétaire général de l'ONU annonce l'engagement de sa liquidation. L'intention était limpide : briser l'élan, geler le texte, rappeler au Maroc qu'on ne réécrit pas impunément un dossier vieux d'un demi-siècle. Le résultat l'est tout autant : le dispositif que Moscou prétendait protéger s'éteint, et avec lui la routine qui servait si commodément de paravent à l'immobilisme. Voilà donc une curieuse opération de sauvetage : le médecin russe voulait empêcher qu'on réforme le traitement du patient ; il a fini par débrancher lui-même l'appareil. Le patient, lui, se porte plutôt bien. C'est le traitement qui est mort. Il fallait une certaine audace pour brandir l'arme suprême du Conseil de sécurité contre un texte… et offrir, en prime, à son adversaire ce qu'il n'aurait jamais obtenu par un vote. Le proverbe marocain trouve ici une résonance presque parfaite : جا يكحّلها عماها Il voulait lui mettre du khôl aux yeux ; il l'a rendue aveugle. Et l'on hésite désormais sur la formule de politesse. Une lettre de remerciements ? Une décoration? Contentons-nous, sobrement : Спасибо, Москва ! – (Merci Moscou) ! Mais attention aux conclusions trop rapides. L'expiration d'un mandat de maintien de la paix ne fait pas disparaître, par enchantement, le différend politique. La question demeure inscrite dans les travaux de décolonisation de l'ONU – ironie supplémentaire pour un territoire dont la seule puissance coloniale, l'Espagne, est partie depuis un demi-siècle. Il faut distinguer la fin d'un dispositif, le règlement d'un différend et la clôture formelle d'un dossier. Ce sont trois réalités différentes, même si l'on voudrait parfois les faire tenir dans un seul communiqué triomphal. Le « R » de référendum : une lettre qui valait trente-cinq ans La querelle diplomatique aura même trouvé son alphabet. Dans MINURSO, le « R » signifie référendum. Un référendum prévu depuis 1991, mais jamais organisé, notamment en raison des désaccords sur le corps électoral et les modalités de consultation. Le projet américain entendait supprimer cette référence du nom de la mission. Moscou y voyait une modification politique majeure. Washington dénonçait au contraire la perpétuation d'un mécanisme devenu inadapté. Ainsi, au Conseil de sécurité, on ne se disputait plus un territoire, un statut ou un avenir institutionnel. On se disputait une lettre. Une lettre devenue monument historique, que les uns voulaient déboulonner et que les autres entendaient conserver sous cloche. Moscou a si bien défendu le « R » qu'il ne reste plus de MINURSO pour le porter. On a sauvé l'enseigne, la boutique a fermé. Il fallait bien que l'absurde administratif trouve un jour son chef-d'œuvre. La Russie a défendu sa position au nom de la nécessité d'une solution négociée et acceptable pour les parties. Les États-Unis, la France et le Royaume-Uni ont regretté son veto, soulignant les conséquences possibles pour le processus politique et la stabilité régionale. Ils n'avaient pas tort sur les conséquences ; ils se sont peut-être trompés sur leur sens. L'Algérie, Moscou et les ambiguïtés du voisinage La réaction algérienne mérite également attention. Alger a critiqué le projet américain, jugé trop favorable au Maroc, et salué l'initiative russe visant à maintenir la MINURSO. Mais la disparition du mandat de cette dernière constitue précisément l'une des conséquences du double échec au Conseil de sécurité. On a applaudi le pompier au moment exact où il coupait l'arrivée d'eau. Il y a là une contradiction politique que les communiqués ne suffisent pas à dissiper. Dans la diplomatie, comme aux échecs, on peut protéger une pièce et perdre une position. Encore faut-il distinguer le coup tactique du résultat stratégique. Moscou, pour sa part, ne saurait être réduite au rôle de simple exécutante des préférences algériennes. La Russie poursuit ses propres intérêts, entretient des relations avec Alger comme avec Rabat et cherche à préserver son influence dans les équilibres régionaux. C'est ce qui rend l'épisode plus savoureux qu'une simple confrontation entre amis et adversaires du Maroc. Le veto, arme suprême des grandes puissances, peut bloquer une résolution. Il ne peut ni immobiliser l'économie, ni suspendre la géographie, ni empêcher les acteurs régionaux de rechercher de nouveaux arrangements. Il peut en revanche, manié avec suffisamment d'assurance, produire exactement l'inverse de l'effet recherché. Le meilleur restait pourtant à venir. Le 1er novembre, au lendemain de l'expiration du mandat, la diplomatie russe publie, par la voix de sa porte-parole Maria Zakharova, un commentaire où elle regrette la fin de la MINURSO, invoque les positions « du Maroc et de l'Algérie » sur l'avenir du territoire et promet de « rester en contact étroit avec [ses] partenaires algériens, marocains et d'autres sur ce dossier ». Algériens, Marocains… Tout est dans cette énumération. Pendant des décennies, Alger s'est présenté comme un simple « pays voisin », un observateur soucieux, presque un spectateur. Le 30 octobre, en saluant le texte russe et en dénonçant le projet américain, il avait déjà laissé voir sa véritable place à la table. Le 1er novembre, c'est son propre allié qui, au détour d'une formule de routine, la met noir sur blanc : l'Algérie figure parmi les interlocuteurs directs du dossier – et même en tête de liste. Lapsus diplomatique ou franchise involontaire, peu importe : le rôle que l'on niait vient d'être consigné par l'ami le plus proche. Le patrimoine coranique offre ici une formule d'une étonnante justesse : (وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا), « Et un témoin issu de sa propre famille témoigna» – Sourate Youssouf, verset 26. Dans le récit de Youssouf, le témoignage décisif ne vient ni de l'accusé ni de ses défenseurs, mais de l'entourage même de celle qui accusait. La formule ne doit pas être prise pour un ralliement russe à la position marocaine. Elle souligne simplement, sur le mode de l'ironie, que lorsque le plus proche partenaire d'Alger range l'Algérie parmi les parties au dossier, la thèse du simple «observateur» perd son meilleur avocat. Après le veto, le véritable travail commence Le Maroc aurait tort de considérer cet épisode comme le dernier acte d'une pièce commencée au siècle précédent. Il pourrait être, au contraire, le premier acte d'une nouvelle séquence. Car l'objectif marocain ne consiste pas simplement à obtenir une résolution de plus, un communiqué supplémentaire ou une photographie diplomatique accompagnée de sourires protocolaires. Il consiste à faire consacrer durablement l'initiative d'autonomie, à transformer le développement des provinces du Sud en stabilité institutionnelle et à sortir progressivement d'une logique de gestion perpétuelle du conflit. La tâche reste considérable. Elle suppose une négociation politique, une consolidation juridique et une diplomatie capable de traiter les désaccords persistants, notamment avec l'Algérie, sans négliger les attentes des populations sahraouies. Le premier combat à venir est donc diplomatique et juridique : transformer une évolution favorable à la position marocaine en règlement international durable. Une chose est de voir disparaître la MINURSO, une autre est d'obtenir la clôture formelle du dossier dans les différentes enceintes concernées, notamment la Quatrième Commission et les organes compétents des Nations unies. On ne ferme pas un dossier international comme on ferme un vieux bureau à cinq heures de l'après-midi. Encore faut-il que les institutions compétentes prennent les décisions nécessaires. Le ciel du Sahara : le dernier vestige d'une administration Le deuxième chantier concerne la gestion de l'espace aérien. Voilà une question moins spectaculaire qu'un veto, mais autrement concrète pour l'avenir des provinces du Sud. L'Espagne continue d'assurer des services de navigation aérienne dans une partie de l'espace concerné, à partir des Canaries – survivance technique d'une époque où Madrid administrait le territoire. La déclaration conjointe maroco-espagnole du 7 avril 2022 avait prévu l'ouverture de discussions sur cette question. En octobre 2026, aucun transfert intégral n'avait encore été officiellement confirmé. Il ne s'agit pas ici d'une question territoriale, mais de responsabilité technique des services de circulation aérienne. Rien n'interdit d'envisager une réorganisation négociée de ces responsabilités opérationnelles, conforme aux règles de l'Organisation de l'aviation civile internationale. Le Maroc peut donc poursuivre un objectif clair : disposer des infrastructures, des compétences et des accords nécessaires pour assurer lui-même une part accrue, puis éventuellement l'ensemble, des services de navigation aérienne concernés. Car une stratégie atlantique ambitieuse suppose aussi des capacités aéronautiques à sa mesure. Le développement de Dakhla, l'essor des liaisons internationales, les investissements touristiques et les futures plateformes logistiques appellent une coordination aérienne moderne, sûre et pleinement opérationnelle. Le ciel n'est pas une affaire de symboles : c'est un espace de responsabilités techniques, de sécurité et de connectivité économique. Lagouira : le dernier kilomètre d'une ambition atlantique Le troisième chantier porte un nom chargé de symboles : Lagouira. «De Tanger à Lagouira» : la formule appartient depuis longtemps à l'imaginaire territorial marocain. Mais à l'extrême sud de la péninsule du Cap Blanc, la situation réelle demeure singulière. Lagouira, inhabitée, se trouve sous contrôle militaire mauritanien depuis plusieurs décennies. Le sujet est revenu dans l'actualité à la faveur des discussions relatives à la délimitation des frontières et des observations rapportées dans le document du secrétaire général de l'ONU en 2026. C'est un enjeu qui appelle moins les proclamations que la diplomatie de précision. Une clarification négociée avec Nouakchott pourrait permettre de traiter les questions de sécurité, de délimitation et de coopération économique, sans compromettre les relations entre deux pays appelés à jouer un rôle important dans l'intégration atlantique. Lagouira ne doit pas devenir un nouveau contentieux immobilisant des générations de diplomates. L'ironie serait cruelle : sortir d'un demi-siècle de blocage pour inaugurer aussitôt un nouveau guichet de réclamations frontalières. Ce serait laisser à d'autres le soin d'offrir, cette fois, un veto gratuit. L'objectif stratégique serait plutôt de transformer cette extrémité géographique en espace de coopération, en tenant compte de la proximité de Nouadhibou, des équilibres mauritaniens et du futur dispositif logistique régional. L'Atlantique : la géographie prend sa revanche sur les résolutions C'est ici que les initiatives royales donnent à la question saharienne une dimension plus large que celle du seul règlement diplomatique. L'Initiative royale visant à faciliter l'accès des pays du Sahel à l'océan Atlantique, annoncée en 2023, entend offrir de nouvelles perspectives commerciales aux États enclavés de la région. Le Mali, le Burkina Faso et le Niger ont confirmé leur intérêt pour cette démarche en avril 2025. Le Tchad participe également aux échanges relatifs à sa mise en œuvre. La future plateforme portuaire de Dakhla Atlantique, la voie express Tiznit-Dakhla et les projets énergétiques figurent parmi les composantes ou les perspectives de cette ambition. En juillet 2026, le chantier de Dakhla Atlantique était annoncé à 65 % d'avancement, avec un achèvement envisagé pour fin 2028 et une mise en service prévue en 2029. Parmi ces projets structurants, le gazoduc Nigeria-Maroc – désormais baptisé gazoduc Afrique Atlantique – occupe une place à part. Long d'environ 6 900 kilomètres, appelé à traverser treize pays de la façade ouest-africaine et estimé à quelque 25 milliards de dollars, il compte parmi les plus vastes projets d'infrastructure du continent. Sur le sol marocain, son tracé emprunte précisément les provinces du Sud : arrivée de la section maritime près de Dakhla, où une station de réception doit la relier au tronçon terrestre, puis stations de compression prévues à Boujdour, Tan-Tan, Agadir et Safi, avant la connexion au réseau national et, au-delà, aux marchés européens. Le projet n'en est pas encore au stade du chantier : la décision finale d'investissement est visée pour la fin de 2026 et une première mise en service est envisagée pour 2031. Mais son tracé dit déjà l'essentiel. Un gazoduc ne se pose pas sur un territoire dont on doute ; il se pose là où l'on entend rester, et où l'on attend que d'autres, de Lagos à Dakar, viennent se raccorder. Ce que des décennies de résolutions n'ont pas tranché, la carte des infrastructures commence à l'écrire. Ces infrastructures ne règlent pas à elles seules un différend diplomatique. Elles modifient cependant les conditions économiques dans lesquelles les États voisins et leurs partenaires envisagent l'avenir de la façade atlantique. Pendant que l'on bloquait des résolutions à New York, on coulait du béton à Dakhla. On sait lequel des deux résiste le mieux au temps. L'enjeu est de faire du Sahara un espace de circulation, d'investissement, de création de valeur et de coopération régionale, plutôt qu'un territoire éternellement défini par la seule controverse diplomatique. Encore faut-il que les bénéfices soient tangibles pour les habitants : emplois, formation, services publics, participation aux décisions et préservation des ressources naturelles. La réussite d'une ambition territoriale ne se mesure pas uniquement à la longueur des routes ou à la profondeur des bassins portuaires. Elle se mesure aussi à la place qu'y occupent les populations. Et maintenant, en attendant… quoi ? Pendant des décennies, certains ont imaginé la question du Sahara comme une représentation sans dernier acte. Un théâtre où l'on attendrait indéfiniment une solution, à la manière des personnages de Samuel Beckett attendant Godot. Godot ne venait jamais. Les rapports, eux, arrivaient ponctuellement. La bureaucratie internationale possède ce talent rare : transformer l'attente en calendrier. Le 30 octobre 2026 n'a pas apporté de règlement définitif. Il a cependant rompu une routine institutionnelle vieille de trente-cinq ans. Le veto russe, brandi pour freiner le Maroc, lui a finalement servi de marchepied. Destiné à empêcher toute transformation du dispositif onusien, il a participé à l'issue que Moscou redoutait le plus : l'expiration du mandat de la mission. Rarement une arme aura été aussi généreuse envers celui qu'elle visait. Le Coran a, pour ces retours de flamme, une formule que l'on ne saurait mieux placer : (وَيَمْكُرُونَ وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ ۖ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ). « Ils complotent, et Allah déjoue leur complot ; et Allah est le meilleur en stratagèmes» – Sourate Al-Anfal, verset 30. L'effet boomerang n'a pas d'autre définition : le calcul qui devait entraver est devenu l'instrument même du dénouement. *Université Cadi AYYAD – Safi – The post En attendant… véto ! appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Université de Carthage | Hommage à trois enseignants de l’INSAT figurant au classement de Stanford
items.description: La Présidente de l’Université de Carthage a rendu hommage, ce matin du 3 novembre 2026, au siège de l’Université, à trois éminents enseignants de l’Institut National des Sciences Appliquées et de Technologie (INSAT) : le Professeur Mokhtar Hamdi, la Professeure Olfa Boubaker et le Maître de Conférences Adnen Arbi. Cet hommage vient saluer leurs remarquables contributions scientifiques ainsi que leur classement parmi les 2 % des scientifiques les plus influents au monde pour l’année 2025, selon le classement établi par l’Université de Stanford. Cette distinction témoigne de l’excellence de leurs travaux de recherche et illustre le rayonnement scientifique de l’Université de Carthage, ainsi que son engagement constant en faveur du développement de la recherche scientifique et de la promotion de l’excellence académique à l’échelle international Communiqué L’article Université de Carthage | Hommage à trois enseignants de l'INSAT figurant au classement de Stanford est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Ogun govt, Ijebu Chiefs clash over Awujale Council as succession crisis deepens
items.description: …State reconstitutes AIAC, insists Adele Oba Awujale group lacks legal backing By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta A fresh controversy has erupted over the administration of Ijebuland following the decision of the Ogun State government to reconstitute the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC), barely a day after traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode announced the dissolution of the council and its replacement with the Adele Oba Awujale in Council. The development has exposed a disagreement between the state government and some traditional authorities over the appropriate legal and customary structure for administering Ijebuland pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale. While the government insists that the AIAC remains the only legally recognised administrative body authorised to oversee the affairs of Ijebuland during the interregnum, the traditional chiefs maintain that the Adele Oba Awujale in Council is rooted in the customs and established traditional practices of the Ijebu people. In a statement issued on Tuesday by the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Hon. Ganiyu Hamzat, the state government said the withdrawal of some members of the AIAC did not invalidate the council or confer legal authority on another body to take over its responsibilities. The government described the AIAC, established in August 2025, as the only legally recognised administrative structure empowered to manage the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland until a new Awujale is appointed and crowned. It specifically clarified that Chief Chris Okunowo and Alhaji Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, had publicly dissociated themselves from the reported mass withdrawal from the council. Dismissing the emergence of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, the government maintained that the body had no legal or customary recognition under the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration or the existing chieftaincy laws of Ogun State. According to Hamzat, neither the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration nor the Ogun State Obas and Chiefs Law 2021 makes provision for an Adele Oba Awujale group or assigns it any recognised responsibility in the administration of the vacant Awujale stool. The government also faulted the reliance on the Chiefs Law of 1957 by some former members to justify the emergence of the new body, arguing that the legislation was enacted before Nigeria’s independence and no longer applied to Ogun State, which had operated under its own laws since its creation in 1976. To support its position, the state government cited a consent judgment delivered by the Ogun State High Court in suit number HCJ/180/2025, involving Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, against the Executive Council of Ogun State and 16 others. It said the judgment affirmed the legality, validity and authority of the AIAC as the administrative body established by the government to oversee the affairs of Ijebu-Ode pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale. The government noted that all members of the council were parties to the suit and had consented to the judgment. It further stated that the court had affirmed that where there was a conflict between the administrative responsibilities of the AIAC and the traditional functions of the Olisa, the authority of the administrative body would take precedence. The statement added that the judgment had not been appealed and remained binding on the parties. Although acknowledging the right of individual members to withdraw from the council, the government warned that such a decision could not confer legal authority on another group to assume the functions of the AIAC. It consequently cautioned members of the public against conducting official transactions or administrative dealings with individuals who had withdrawn from the council in their purported capacity as members of an alternative administrative body. The government also urged the former members to refrain from actions capable of violating the law or threatening peace and stability in Ijebuland. Consequently, it announced the reconstitution of the AIAC to ensure continuity in the administration of the ancient town. The reconstituted council comprises Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, as Chairman; Chief Chris Okunowo, Bobasuwa, as Secretary; Prof. Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso; Chief Stephen O. Bakare, Babalaje; and Chief Alade Shote, Otun Balogun, as members. The government said the council would continue to discharge its legally recognised administrative and traditional responsibilities until a new Awujale was appointed and crowned. ……..Chiefs insist on traditional authority However, the government’s position came against the backdrop of a resolution adopted on Monday by traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode to dissolve the AIAC and replace it with the Adele Oba Awujale in Council. The resolution was reached at a meeting involving the Ilamuren, Pampa, the Odi and other traditional chiefs of Ijebu-Ode, where the leaders reportedly agreed that members of the existing AIAC should step down from their positions and assume membership of the newly constituted body. The state government had established the AIAC in August 2025, about a month after the death of the 91-year-old Awujale, Oba Sikiru Adetona, in July 2025, to manage the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland during the transition period. The initial administrative arrangement was chaired by Chief Folorunso Kuku, the Ogbeni Oja of Ijebuland and co-founder of EKO Hospital, Lagos, who is also designated as one of the Ilamuren. But in a resolution signed by the Chairman of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, Olo’rgun Dr Sonny Kuku, the traditional chiefs said their decision to replace the AIAC was informed by their interpretation of the existing traditional and statutory frameworks governing the Awujale chieftaincy institution. They argued that the Ogun State Chiefs Law 2021 did not expressly establish an Awujale Regency Council or prescribe a general procedure for appointing a regent during an interregnum. The chiefs, however, maintained that the Chiefs Law and the 1957 Declaration provided a framework for recognising customary arrangements, including the traditional institution of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council. The resolution stated: “Upon consideration of the applicable traditional and statutory framework, it was observed that the Ogun State Chiefs Law of 2021 does not expressly establish an Awujale Regency Council, nor does it prescribe a general procedure for the appointment of a Regent.” It added: “It was further noted that the Chiefs Law and Declaration of 1957 provide an existing framework within which customary declarations are made and recognised, including the traditional institution of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.” Explaining the decision to replace the AIAC, the chiefs said: “In view of the foregoing, a motion was moved and unanimously adopted that all members of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC) should formally step down from their existing positions and transition into the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.” They further declared that the new body would assume responsibility for the administration of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum. “Consequently, the Adele Oba Awujale in Council shall henceforth assume responsibility for the administration of the affairs of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum and exercise, on an interim basis, such administrative powers and functions as may appropriately be required in the absence of the Awujale, subject to applicable laws and established customs and traditions,” the resolution stated. The 14-member Adele Oba Awujale in Council comprises Dr Sonny Kuku, who holds the Ogbeni Oja title; Chief Rasheed Adesanya, Olisa; Chief O.B. Okuboyejo, Obasewa; Chief Chris Funmilola Okunowo, Bobasuwa; and Chief Prof. Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso. Other members are Chief Oluwaranti Lekan Osifeso, Olootu Olowa; Chief Jimi Lawal, Olotu Ifore; Chief Kunle Ogunade, Apebi; Chief Mrs B.O. Osibogun, Iyalode; Chief Adegoke Balogun, Jaginrin; Chief Agboola Alausa, Balogun; Chief Abimbola Okenla, Kakanfo; Chief Adebisi Adaran, Ogbeni Odi Awujale; and Chief Ayotunde Ola Odulaja, Lapoekun. The traditional leaders described the arrangement as a recognised customary administrative structure designed to ensure continuity and stability in Ijebu-Ode while the process of selecting and installing a substantive Awujale continues. “The Adele Oba Awujale in Council shall henceforth serve as the recognised traditional administrative body for the management of the affairs of Ijebu-Ode throughout the interregnum, in accordance with applicable laws, customary practices and the established traditions of Ijebuland,” the statement declared. The chiefs also maintained that their decision was anchored on the customs and longstanding cultural practices of the Ijebu people, particularly those governing the Awujale chieftaincy institution. “Our position is firmly rooted in the ancient customs, established cultural practices and time-honoured traditions of the Ijebu people, particularly as they relate to the Awujale Chieftaincy Institution,” they stated. They added that the resolution was intended to protect the integrity of the traditional institution and preserve the historical framework of Ijebuland until a new Awujale emerges. items.title: Changes to Chile’s Human Rights Institute Risk Leaving Victims Behind
items.description: Click to expand Image Chile's President Jose Antonio Kast waves on his inauguration day at Congress in Valparaiso, Chile, March 11, 2026. © 2026 Esteban Felix/AP Photo Chilean President José Antonio Kast introduced in Congress on October 19 a proposal to change the country’s National Human Rights Institute. Founded in 2009 as an autonomous state body, the institute has worked to promote and protect human rights in Chile, including by taking legal action on behalf of human rights abuse victims. If passed, the legislation would weaken some of the tools the institute uses to protect human rights and diminish its independence. The bill would remove the institute’s eleven-member board of directors, replacing them with a new five-member transitional board that would draft new bylaws for the institute. Unlike the current board, which has four members who were selected directly by civil society groups, the new transitional board would be proposed by the president, approved by the Senate, and would have no members selected directly by civil society. This sits uneasily with the standards set out in the Principles relating to the Status of National Human Rights Institutions (the Paris Principles), which recommend that members be independent from the government and selected through a process that ensures broad civil society representation. According to a financial report by the Finance Ministry’s Budget Office, the proposal would also reduce the institute’s staff. The number of staff members in the institute’s regional offices outside of Santiago de Chile would be cut in half, and the number of lawyers in the institute’s protection unit, who handle the institute’s legal actions, would be reduced by 70 percent. As a result, people in many parts of Chile could lose access to in-person assistance from the institute. The proposed legislation would also end the institute’s ability to represent victims in criminal cases—a power it has often used in cases of torture, ill treatment, or human trafficking. That would mean that victims who cannot afford a lawyer would lose legal support and would rely on prosecutors to decide whether to pursue their case and how to move it forward. The National Human Rights Institute itself has welcomed other parts of the bill meant to improve its transparency and governance but has warned that some aspects of the bill would undermine its work. Chile’s Congress should reexamine these worrying provisions and make sure the institute can protect the rights of all Chileans.

items.title: Tinubu fulfils pledge as Super Falcons receive $100,000 cash rewards
items.description: The Federal Government has paid cash rewards to players, coaches and officials of the Super Falcons following their victory at the 2025 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), completing the reward package promised by President Bola Tinubu. The National Sports Commission (NSC) disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Head of Press and Public Relations, Zira Zakka Nagga. According to the commission, each player received the naira equivalent of $100,000, while each coach and official received the equivalent of $50,000. The team had earlier received the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON) and three-bedroom apartments. The Chairman of the NSC, Shehu Dikko, thanked Tinubu for fulfilling his pledge, saying the President had directed that all aspects of the reward package be delivered within a reasonable time. “The Super Falcons made Nigeria proud, and Mr President has honoured his commitment to them in full. This means a great deal to the team and to Nigerian sports,” Dikko said. He said the President’s action marked a departure from previous experiences in which some Nigerian athletes waited years to receive promised rewards. “Some of our sports heroes endured years of waiting for promises to be fulfilled. President Tinubu has shown that things can be done differently,” he said. Dikko added that the fulfilment of the pledge would encourage athletes to represent the country with confidence that their efforts would be recognised. He also said the gesture would inspire young Nigerians, particularly girls aspiring to pursue careers in sports. The NSC chairman recalled that Nigeria’s senior women’s basketball team, D’Tigress, received similar cash rewards in September 2026 after winning their fifth consecutive FIBA Women’s AfroBasket title in 2025. Each D’Tigress player received the naira equivalent of $100,000, while officials received $50,000 each. The team had also received three-bedroom apartments and national honours. Dikko also cited the completion of rewards for the Super Eagles following their silver-medal finish at the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations, held in Côte d’Ivoire in 2024. He thanked the Ministers of Finance, Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, and Housing and Urban Development for their roles in completing the reward package. “Delivering these rewards required close cooperation across government. We appreciate the Honourable Ministers and their teams for working with the Commission to complete the necessary processes,” he said. The commission congratulated the Super Falcons’ players, coaches and officials on their achievement, urging Nigerian athletes preparing for future competitions to draw encouragement from the fulfilment of the President’s promises. It quoted Tinubu as saying: “My promise to every Nigerian athlete is: make Nigeria proud, and come back to a grateful nation.” The post Tinubu fulfils pledge as Super Falcons receive $100,000 cash rewards appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: La ministre de la Jeunesse et des Sports, Djirèye Clotilde Coly, a effectué, mardi 3 novembre, une visite sur plusieurs sites des JOJ Dakar 2026. L’occasion de saluer la médaille de bronze remportée par le judoka Matar Diop et de relever la qualité de l’organisation ainsi que le niveau des compétitions. Au Centre d’exposition de Diamniadio, où se déroulent les épreuves de wushu, la ministre a assisté aux démonstrations en présence du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Elle s’est réjouie de la qualité du spectacle et de l’accueil réservé aux délégations. Même appréciation après les rencontres de badminton, dont elle a souligné l’intensité et le niveau technique. Au-delà des performances sportives, Dakar 2026 donne à voir une autre facette du Sénégal. La cérémonie d’ouverture, organisée au stade Abdoulaye Wade, a placé la culture nationale et africaine au cœur du spectacle. Entre tableaux de lutte, prestations musicales, défilé des délégations et allumage de la vasque par la jeune judokate Aïcha Diop, le pays a voulu partager son identité avec le monde. Cette première édition des JOJ organisée en Afrique réunit plus de 2 700 athlètes venus de plus de 200 pays, autour de 35 disciplines. Pour la ministre, l’enjeu est aussi de mobiliser les Sénégalais autour de cet événement. items.title: Réadaptation physique : Une conférence régionale pour l’inclusion des personnes en situation de handicap
items.description: Lomé, 3 nov. (ATOP) – La délégation du Comité international de la Croix-Rouge (CICR) à Lomé, organise du 3 au 6 novembre, une conférence régionale sur la promotion et l’intégration de la réadaptation physique, dans les systèmes de santé en Afrique francophone. Cet événement est couplé du lancement officiel du projet d’Education en réadaptation pour l’Afrique francophone (PERAF). Il est initié en collaboration avec ses partenaires, et sous les auspices des ministères en charge de la Santé, de l’Enseignement supérieur, et des Solidarités. D onner de la visibilité à la problématique du handicap Cette conférence vise à promouvoir le Droit international humanitaire et à améliorer l’accès et l’inclusion des personnes en situation de handicap en Afrique de l’Ouest. Il s’agit de donner de la visibilité à la problématique du handicap et de mobiliser les décideurs politiques. Il est question également d’influencer l’intégration et l’ancrage des services de réadaptation directement dans les systèmes nationaux de santé publique dans les pays francophones de l’Afrique de l’ouest. Il s’agit également de permettre aux experts, praticiens et centres orthopédiques de la sous-région d’échanger sur les meilleures pratiques de prise en charge clinique. A travers la réadaptation physique, il s’agit de permettre aux femmes, aux hommes et à aux enfants de bénéficier des moyens nécessaires pour retrouver ou améliorer leur mobilité, préserver leur autonomie et participer pleinement à la vie économique et sociale. Le ministre de la Santé, de l’Hygiène publique, de la Couverture sanitaire universelle et des Assurances, Jean-Marie Koffi Ewonoulé Tessi, a indiqué que « la réadaptation physique est donc bien plus qu’une question technique. Elle est une exigence de santé publique, un impératif d’équité et un investissement dans le développement humain ». Il a fait savoir que « C’est pour cela que nous devons donc poursuivre nos efforts pour que les services de réadaptation soient davantage reconnus, organisés et progressivement intégrés dans les dispositifs de prise en charge, selon des modalités adaptées à nos réalités nationales ». M. Tessi a dit attendre de ces échanges, des propositions réalistes, des partenariats renforcés et des feuilles de route nationales clairement définies, assorties de responsabilités et de mécanismes de suivi en faveur du développement de la réadaptation physique. Le PERAF, une réponse structurante à l’insuffisance de professionnels Le Projet d’éducation en réadaptation pour l’Afrique francophone est un programme de formation, une réponse structurante à l’insuffisance de professionnels hautement qualifiés en sciences des prothèses et orthèses. À travers le développement d’une formation supérieure de niveau master en sciences des prothèses et orthèses à Lomé, ce projet entend former des experts cliniciens et des enseignants capables, à leur tour, de transmettre des compétences spécialisées. Le PERAF est ainsi porteur d’une double promesse : renforcer l’expertise africaine et améliorer, à terme, l’accès des populations à des services de réadaptation de qualité. Le PERAF constitue une opportunité de renforcer les capacités pédagogiques, scientifiques et institutionnelles des établissements de formation. Il offre également la perspective de consolider le positionnement du Togo comme un pôle régional de référence dans la formation supérieure des professionnels en sciences des prothèses et orthèses. Le ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche, Prof. Gado Tchangbedji a formulé le voeu que le PERAF soit non seulement un projet qui forme des compétences, mais surtout une initiative qui bâtit des institutions, consolide l’expertise africaine et ouvre de nouvelles perspectives de dignité et d’autonomie aux populations. ATOP/KYA/AJA

items.title: Pakistan successfully tests its first indigenously developed air-to-air missile Fa’az: ISPR
items.description: Pakistan on Tuesday performed a successful flight test of the country’s first indigenously developed air-to-air missile, Fa’az, “marking another significant milestone in the advancement of national aerospace and defence capabilities”, the military’s media wing said . According to a statement by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the missile is equipped with a state-of-the-art terminal guidance system and can engage enemy targets at longer ranges. “Fa’az will significantly enhance [the] operational flexibility of [the] Pakistan Air Force, further strengthening the country’s overall defence posture. The successful flight test underscores the technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance achieved by Pakistan’s defence industry,” the statement added. The launch was witnessed by senior military officers, scientists and engineers involved in the development of the system, the ISPR said. It added that President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and the service chiefs congratulated the scientists. Pakistan’s first indigenously developed air-to-air missile, Fa’az, is test-launched from a JF-17 fighter jet in this video released on Nov 3, 2026. — Screengrab via X/DGPR_PAF Meanwhile, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi issued a statement congratulating the nation on the test. “Our scientists and engineers have once again achieved a remarkable feat that makes the nation proud,” the ministry quoted him as saying. “The successful test of the indigenously developed Fa’az missile marks a significant advancement in the field of defence. “We are all proud of Pakistan’s distinguished scientists and engineers.” Pakistan successfully tested two surface-to-surface missiles last month; the Fatah-2 extended range (ER) hypersonic ballistic missile was tested on Oct 13, and the indigenously developed extended version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile was tested a week before that. ISPR said that the Fatah-2 ER is equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics. “It is capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating [the] enemy’s missile defence systems due to its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features,” it added. For Fatah-IV ER, ISPR said: “Equipped with advanced avionics and state-of-the-art navigational aids, the weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.” It noted that the test “also validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability”.

items.title: Ethiopian Authorities Suspend Independent Newspaper
items.description: Click to expand Image A man reads the Ethiopian Reporter in Addis Ababa on December 11, 2019. © 2019 Eduardo Soteras/AFP via Getty Images In what has become the new normal, the Ethiopian government has silenced yet another independent media outlet. The Ethiopian Media Authority announced in a November 2 Facebook post that it is indefinitely suspending the print and online license of the Reporter, one of Ethiopia’s oldest media institutions. Publishing in English and Amharic, the Reporter is also the country’s last privately owned Amharic newspaper. Stating that the suspension would take effect immediately, the Media Authority accused the Reporter of violating the country’s laws and media ethics by repeatedly publishing content that was against “national interests.” The authority added that the outlet published “distorted content that negatively affects foreign investment, tourism, and diplomacy.” The action is part of the government’s ongoing assault on the media and civic space in the country and points toward increasing use of vague claims about “national interests” to shut down any critical reporting. Since 2025, Ethiopian authorities have banned numerous media outlets, deported foreign correspondents, and targeted local journalists through arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, and office raids. In October, undercover police detained journalists Samuel Getachew and Amanuel Gebremedhin, charging them with reporting news that would cause disruptions in Addis Ababa, the capital. The two were jailed for eight days. The Reporter, one of the few remaining independent outlets in the country, hasn’t been spared. Authorities have arrested its journalists, while the outlet itself has been under government pressure. Days before the suspension, the Reporter published an editorial warning that Ethiopia’s privately owned press was “navigating one of its most precarious periods in history” and calling for immediate reforms to prevent its total collapse. The Ethiopian government should heed the warning; the country’s concerned partners should urge the government to immediately reverse course.

items.title: GACL’s GH¢30m dividend Is manufactured and misleading – Africa Policy Lens
items.description: The Africa Policy Lens (APL) says the much-publicised GH¢30 million dividend by the Ghana Airports Company Limited (GACL) to Government is manufactured and does not reflect operational performance. In a statement issued by its Research Directorate, APL said it had examined GACL’s 2025 Audited Accounts as presented at its 11th Annual General Meeting and concluded that the dividend is being misrepresented as evidence of a turnaround. “While the Ghana Airports Company Limited and the government seek to present this as evidence of a dramatic turnaround, the GACL report itself exposes serious underlying weaknesses,” the statement said. APL listed four findings to back its claim. First, it said GACL’s core business is shrinking. According to APL, core operating revenue fell by 9.15% from GH¢2.02 billion in 2024 to GH¢1.83 billion in 2025. Second, it argued that profit was propped by non-cash revaluation. APL said the declared profit of GH¢354.6 million was significantly supported by GH¢578 million in Other Operating Gains, largely revaluation gains, which it described as accounting entries and not cash from passenger traffic. Third, APL pointed to loss-making regional airports. It cited the Managing Director of GACL, Mrs. Yvonne Nana Afriyie Opare, as being emphatic that domestic business operations and all regional airports are not yet profitable. “In effect, Kotoka International Airport continues to subsidise Kumasi, Tamale, Sunyani, Wa and Takoradi,” APL added. Fourth, APL said the dividend was only possible because of a debt holiday, adding that what aided the dividend was the restructuring of GACL’s syndicated loan with an eight-year extension and a one-year moratorium on principal repayment, which provided temporary liquidity relief. “A dividend that represents less than 10% of declared profit, paid after 18 years of no dividend, and enabled by a debt repayment holiday and non-cash revaluation, should not be celebrated as efficiency or profitability,” APL said. The think tank has called on GACL and the Ministry of Transport to publish the full audited statements, disclose the cash-backed portion of the profit, and explain why domestic operations remain loss-making after years of investment. It also called on Parliament to investigate the matter. “Ghanaians deserve airports that are operationally viable with less levies, not dividends that are manufactured through accounting and debt restructuring,” said the statement.

items.title: Army neutralises 2 kidnappers in Kogi follow-up operation
items.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two suspected kidnappers and recovered two AK-47 rifles and thousands of rounds of ammunition during a follow-up operation in Kogi State. The operation took place on Tuesday in Edimogbo Forest, Igalamela-Odolu Local Government Area, as troops continued efforts to track fleeing suspects following a raid on a suspected kidnappers’ hideout in the same forest on Monday. The Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 12 Composite Brigade, Lt. Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday in Lokoja. Abdullahi said troops sustained their operations in the forest to locate fleeing suspects, clear remaining hideouts and restrict the movement of criminal elements. He said the troops made contact with the suspects during the follow-up operation and engaged them, forcing them to retreat. “The encounter resulted in the neutralisation of two kidnappers, while others fled into the surrounding forest,” he said. A subsequent search of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, seven magazines, 438 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 ammunition and 4,725 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. Other items recovered included two bandoliers, two mobile phones and a power bank. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that troops had dismantled a suspected kidnappers’ camp in the forest during Monday’s operation, recovering about 1,000 rounds of ammunition and six motorcycles. Abdullahi said Tuesday’s operation had consolidated the gains of the earlier raid, adding that troops remained committed to sustaining pressure on criminal groups. He said the brigade would continue operations to protect lives and property and support efforts to restore lasting peace across Kogi State. The post Army neutralises 2 kidnappers in Kogi follow-up operation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pakistan’s new UN envoy presents credentials to secretary general in New York
items.description: UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan’s newly appointed Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, presented his credentials to UN Secretary General António Guterres at UN Headquarters in New York on Tuesday. During the meeting, Ambassador Shah reaffirmed Islamabad’s commitment to multilateralism, the UN Charter and the organisation’s work in promoting international peace and security, sustainable development and human rights. He also conveyed the greetings of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy PM Ishaq Dar. Guterres reciprocated the greetings and appreciated Pakistan’s positive and constructive contributions to the UN. A senior career diplomat, Ambassador Shah had served as Pakistan’s ambassador to the Netherlands since March 2025, and was posted in Nepal from 2020 to 2022. He also served as the deputy head of Mission at Pakistan’s High Commission in New Delhi from 2016 to 2020, including as acting high commissioner. Shah has considerable experience in multilateral diplomacy and international law. From 2008 to 2013, he served as a legal officer at the UN Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate in New York. Prior to that, from 2002 to 2006, he was posted at Pakistan’s Permanent Mission to the UN in New York, where he covered the General Assembly’s Sixth Committee and participated in negotiations on UN Security Council (UNSC) and General Assembly resolutions. He also served as an additional secretary for UN and Organisation of Islamic Cooperation affairs at Pakistan’s foreign ministry from November 2022 to February 2025. Shah holds an LL.M. from Harvard Law School and an LL.B. from the University of Peshawar’s Khyber Law College. He also holds a postgraduate diploma in international law from the Institute of Social Studies, Erasmus University, The Hague. He co-authored a research paper on the legislative powers of the UNSC, published in 2005. The former UN envoy, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, left New York last month to take up his new responsibilities as Pakistan’s foreign secretary , ending his two-year assignment as the country’s permanent representative to the UN. He paid his farewell call on Guterres on Sept 30.

items.title: Attijariwafa bank et sa néobanque Simple. enrichissent leur offre de paiement mobile avec Samsung Pay
items.description: Dans le cadre de sa stratégie de transformation digitale et d’innovation au service de l’expérience client, le groupe Attijariwafa bank, en partenariat avec Samsung Maroc, annonce le déploiement de Samsung Pay auprès des clients d’Attijariwafa bank et de sa néobanque Simple. Disponible en avant-première depuis le 2 novembre, à l’occasion de son lancement officiel le 3 novembre, cette solution vient enrichir l’offre de paiement mobile du Groupe, en proposant une expérience de paiement simple, rapide et sécurisée. Grâce à la technologie NFC, Samsung Pay permet aux clients disposant d’un smartphone Samsung compatible de régler leurs achats directement depuis leur téléphone, sans utiliser leur carte physique Visa ou Mastercard, auprès des commerçants équipés de terminaux de paiement sans contact compatibles. Disponible pour l’ensemble des produits d’Attijariwafa bank et de Simple. , la solution repose également sur la tokenisation, une technologie qui remplace les données sensibles de la carte par un identifiant numérique sécurisé (token), évitant ainsi leur transmission au commerçant lors du paiement. Ce lancement illustre l’engagement continu du groupe Attijariwafa bank en faveur de l’innovation et de la digitalisation des services bancaires. À travers l’enrichissement de son écosystème de paiement, le Groupe poursuit son ambition de proposer des solutions innovantes, accessibles et sécurisées, adaptées aux nouveaux usages et aux besoins quotidiens de ses clients. items.title: Toluwanisings: Oyo Police summon wife, father, friends as parties sign peace deal
items.description: The Oyo State Police Command has brokered peace between the family and associates of late Nigerian singer Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, following disagreements over his burial arrangements. The intervention comes amid allegations of conspiracy, defamation of character and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace, which reportedly generated public exchanges between parties on social media and other communication platforms. In a statement on Tuesday, the Command said the Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, received information about the dispute on October 28, 2026, and subsequently directed the parties to appear at the Command Headquarters in Eleyele, Ibadan, for an intervention. The police said the meeting, which was held on November 3, resulted in the parties signing a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police. Those involved included the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunni Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as his personal assistant and other representatives. According to the statement, the parties agreed to maintain peace, exhibit good behaviour and refrain from actions capable of escalating tensions surrounding the singer’s death and burial arrangements. The statement reads, “Consequently, at the conclusion of the engagement held today, 3rd November 2026, all parties, comprising the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; his friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunni Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as the deceased’s personal assistant and other representatives, entered into and signed a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police. “Under the terms of the undertaking, all parties agreed to maintain peace and be of good behaviour, refrain from any act capable of causing a breach of the peace, and discontinue public exchanges, interviews and discussions capable of inflaming tensions or aggravating the existing disagreement surrounding the unfortunate demise of the singer and related issues. “Furthermore, the parties expressly undertook to discontinue the dissemination of information, narratives, allegations and publications relating to the matter through social media platforms, print media, radio, blogs and other communication channels, including publications made through their respective proxies, agents, associates and representatives. They equally agreed not to grant interviews, provide access or facilitate engagements with individuals or media platforms for the purpose of further disseminating such narratives. In addition, each party undertook to direct their respective proxies and associates to desist from making, sponsoring, amplifying or circulating publications capable of reigniting the disagreement or undermining the peace agreement. “In reinforcing the terms of the undertaking, the Commissioner of Police warned that the agreement must be respected by all parties and extended to their proxies, agents, associates and representatives. He cautioned that no individual should take advantage of the unfortunate circumstances surrounding the singer’s demise to instigate hostility, promote unsubstantiated allegations or engage in conduct capable of disrupting public peace. Any person whose actions constitute an offence under applicable laws will be arrested and prosecuted accordingly.” The Command also appealed to members of the public, bloggers and media practitioners to exercise restraint and avoid amplifying unverified information capable of reigniting tensions. It urged all concerned to respect the commitments made during the peace meeting, adding that any conduct independently amounting to a criminal offence would be addressed in accordance with the law. items.title: PLF 2027 : ce qui pourrait changer pour le retour des Algériens de l’étranger
items.description: L'Assemblée populaire nationale (APN) a repris ses travaux en séances plénières lundi 2 novembre pour examiner le projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027. Le ministre des Finances Mohamed Lamine Lebbou a présenté les grandes lignes du PLF 2027 et la Commission des Finances de l’APN a présenté 26 amendements dont un concerne les Algériens de l’étranger. Selon lui, les recettes budgétaires devraient dépasser 9251,1 milliards de dinars, en hausse de 7,4 % par rapport à 2026. Pour les dépenses, elles devraient atteindre 17.251,6 milliards de dinars en autorisations d'engagement (AE) et à 17.882,6 milliards de dinars en crédits de paiement (CP). Le PLF 2027 prévoit un taux de croissance de 4,2%. Pour les dépenses de transfert (subventions), le PLF 2027 prévoit 4.356,64 milliards de dinars en AE et de 4.415,35 milliards de dinars en CP. PLF 2027 : un amendement propose un « dispositif » spécial pour les Algériens de l’étranger De son côté, la commission des finances et du budget de l'Assemblée populaire nationale (APN) a proposé 26 amendements au PLF 2027, selon son rapport préliminaire. Parmi lesquels, le rapporteur de la commission a cité l'article 169 bis. Ce dernier propose la mise en place d'un « dispositif spécial » au profit des Algériens établis à l'étranger depuis au « moins trois années sans interruption » et souhaitant revenir définitivement au pays. Cet amendement propose de leur permettre d'importer les équipements et le matériel liés à leur activité économique ou professionnelle exercée à l'étranger, « tout en étant exonérés des procédures de contrôle du commerce extérieur et des changes, ainsi que des droits et taxes de douane », selon le texte. Cette incitation fiscale vise à faciliter le retour des Algériens de l’étranger dans un contexte où l’Algérie cherche à attirer des compétences et des entrepreneurs basés à l’étranger pour participer au développement de son économie. L’article PLF 2027 : ce qui pourrait changer pour le retour des Algériens de l’étranger est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Achimota 1986 Year Group refurbishes historic Aggrey Chapel to preserve school heritage
items.description: The 1986 year group of Achimota School has refurbished the institution’s historic Aggrey Chapel as part of activities marking 40 years since its members left the school, in a project aimed at preserving the landmark building and improving worship conditions for students. The renovation, officially handed over on Tuesday, November 3, forms the group’s legacy project for its Ruby Anniversary and reflects its commitment to giving back to its alma mater under the tagline, #StrongerTogether. The project was designed with cost efficiency in mind, with the renovated chapel intended to be low-maintenance and self-sustaining. It is also expected to generate modest revenue to support its upkeep without placing an additional financial burden on the school’s resources. Construction cost approximately GH¢1.2 million. Speaking at the handover ceremony, Achimota School Headmaster, Ebenezer Graham Acquaah, commended the alumni for what he described as a significant demonstration of gratitude, restoration and commitment to the institution’s heritage. He said the intervention had restored the chapel’s former glory while preserving its historical character. Named after the school’s co-founder, Dr Kwegyir Aggrey, the chapel has served as the spiritual heart of Achimota for 99 years, providing generations of students with a place for prayer, worship and spiritual development. Mr Acquaah noted that the facility had played an important role in students’ religious formation, including baptisms, confirmations and spiritual preparation, as well as offering a place of reflection before the start of each school week. However, years of exposure to the weather had left the building deteriorated, with broken pews, an inadequate sound system and faded paintwork making worship increasingly uncomfortable. The renovation involved electrical rewiring, the installation of modern sound systems and fans, new altar cloths, improvements to some of the pews and repainting of the chapel’s interior and exterior. The Headmaster expressed appreciation to the year group’s executives and members in Ghana and abroad, acknowledging contributions of all sizes. He said the project reflected the school’s motto, Ut Omnes Unum Sint (That All May Be One), and demonstrated that Achimotans remained committed to their roots. He assured the alumni that school management would maintain the facility, while the Chaplaincy Council would ensure it continued to serve its intended religious purpose. President of the 1986 year group, Sena Siaw-Boateng, disclosed that members had to finance the bulk of the project after anticipated external funding failed to materialise. She explained that the original funding arrangement envisaged external donors providing about 80 per cent of the cost, with members contributing the remaining 20 per cent. However, the group had to return to its members for additional support when the expected external contributions did not come through. Mrs Siaw-Boateng described the renovation as a transformative undertaking intended to improve worship conditions and strengthen students’ spiritual lives. She recounted that members initially held differing views on the focus of their legacy project, with some proposing the construction of a staff common room while others favoured an intervention that would benefit a wider section of the school community. She credited discussions among members, particularly the views of Kweku Gyasi, with helping to shape the decision to renovate the chapel. The project also involved extending the works beyond the initial plans following advice from the school board and project committee. In addition to the chapel renovation, the year group installed a disability access ramp at the chapel and another at the school’s old assembly hall to improve accessibility for persons with disabilities. Mrs Siaw-Boateng stressed that maintaining a historic structure such as the Aggrey Chapel required considerable attention and resources, and appealed to school management to take renewed ownership of its upkeep. She proposed the appointment of a dedicated maintenance officer to oversee the facility, given its frequent use and the inevitable wear and tear. She further disclosed that the group had established a maintenance fund in March, with the money secured in an asset fund specifically for the chapel’s upkeep. Members intend to make further contributions and encourage other donors to support the fund. Board Chair of Achimota School, Professor Ernest Aryeetey, also praised the year group for its commitment and willingness to compromise throughout the project. He said the successful completion of the renovation demonstrated the importance of dialogue and cooperation between alumni, school management and the governing board, particularly when disagreements arise over the nature and scope of projects. Although the final outcome differed from what the board would have preferred, he said the parties had been able to resolve their differences through discussion. Professor Aryeetey congratulated the alumni for accommodating the board’s concerns without abandoning their commitment to the project. He expressed hope that the renovation would serve as the beginning of broader efforts to improve worship facilities at the school, while indicating that plans for a bigger chapel could still be pursued in the future. The 1986 year group is a community of approximately 350 former students whose shared experiences at Achimota have sustained bonds of friendship and solidarity for four decades. As part of its Ruby Anniversary celebrations, the group also honoured clergy whose guidance shaped students’ formative years at the school. Those recognised included Rev. Canon L. Ankrah, a former headmaster, Reverend Pobi and Archbishop Charles Gabriel Archbishop Palmer-Buckle, the project’s patron bishop and Metropolitan Archbishop of Cape Coast of the Catholic Church of Ghana. Mrs Siaw-Boateng urged the clergy to continue supporting the spiritual formation of students, emphasising the importance of moral and religious guidance. The group also paid tribute to 27 departed classmates, whose memories, it said, remained an important part of its shared history. The refurbishment of the Aggrey Chapel, the group said, represents its desire to preserve Achimota’s heritage while contributing to the school’s future. For the alumni, the project is not only a physical restoration of a historic building but also a lasting expression of the friendship, unity and shared responsibility captured in their anniversary message: #StrongerTogether.

items.title: Armah-Kofi Buah challenges KNUST engineering students to lead the fight against galamsey
items.description: The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, has challenged geological engineering students at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) to use their professional expertise to develop practical solutions to illegal mining and environmental destruction. He said the country’s future depended largely on the decisions and actions of the current generation, urging the students to take an active role in protecting Ghana’s natural resources. Speaking at a seminar organised by the Geological Engineering Students Society (GESS) on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, Mr Armah-Kofi Buah said the time for engineers to join the fight against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, was now. He called on the students to move beyond discussions and contribute their technical knowledge to efforts to address the environmental damage caused by irresponsible mining activities. “We in this generation have a responsibility,” he said, adding that the fight against illegal mining must involve students, particularly those whose training is directly connected to the country’s geological and mineral resources. Drawing on his experience in public service, particularly his oversight of Ghana’s oil and gas industry, the Minister said national development often required leaders to make difficult decisions despite resistance and practical challenges. He recalled the challenges associated with establishing the country’s gas infrastructure, including difficulties with land allocation and litigation, during a period when Ghana was struggling with persistent power outages and the need for reliable electricity. He said those obstacles did not deter the government from pursuing the establishment of the Atuabo Gas Processing Plant. According to him, the facility became an important intervention in reducing the cost of power generation. Using the experience to encourage the students, he said leadership required confronting problems and finding solutions rather than allowing difficulties to derail important projects. “When you face challenges, look for where the challenges are coming from and solve them,” he advised. Mr Armah-Kofi Buah also cited the introduction of a sliding-scale royalty regime in the mining sector as an example of difficult policy decisions intended to increase government revenue from mineral resources. He said such decisions were necessary to ensure that Ghana derived greater value from its natural wealth. He further disclosed that securing a US$7 million investment for KNUST’s Petroleum Engineering Department had required considerable effort, negotiations and persistence. Engineers urged to help tackle environmental destruction Turning to illegal mining, the Minister expressed concern about the destruction of forest reserves, air pollution and contamination of water bodies. He said the scale of environmental damage required sustained national attention, effective enforcement and the involvement of professionals with the technical knowledge to develop lasting solutions. He urged the students to apply their training to the challenges confronting the mining sector rather than remain on the sidelines. The Minister also pointed to reforms under the government’s new mining legislation, saying they were intended to strengthen the regulation and governance of mineral resources while ensuring that mining communities benefited more meaningfully from resource extraction. He said the reforms sought to address the longstanding concerns of communities that host mining operations. Advice on professional responsibility Mr Armah-Kofi Buah urged the students to remain focused on their goals, develop the courage to make difficult decisions and avoid being distracted by the desire to impress others. “Focus on decisions and never look back,” he advised.
